# Category: RERA Compliance & Builder Diligence

## How do I tell whether a property ad is RERA-compliant?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/advertisement-rera-number-check/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Check three things. The project must be registered before it's advertised (section 3). The ad must prominently show the Karnataka RERA website address and the project's registration number (section 11(2)). And the number must match the project and phase on the portal. If you pay relying on a false ad, section 12 gives you a right to compensation.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Must every property ad in Karnataka show a RERA number?**: For a project that requires registration, section 11(2) requires the ad to show the registration number and the Authority's website address prominently.
- **Is "RERA applied" in an ad acceptable?**: Section 3 bars advertising or booking a project that needs registration before it's registered. An ad without a granted registration number is a warning sign.
- **Can I get my money back if the brochure was misleading?**: Section 12 says that if you paid relying on a false statement in an ad or model flat and choose to withdraw, you get your entire investment back with interest and compensation.
- **Does the RERA number cover the whole project?**: Not always. Where a project is built in phases, each phase is registered separately, so check the number covers the tower and phase you're buying in.
- **Where can I complain about a misleading property ad?**: To Karnataka RERA under section 31. Keep a dated copy of the ad and any payment receipts.

---

## What counts as &#x27;affordable housing&#x27; for the 1% GST rate?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/affordable-housing-gst-1-percent-definition/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** In Bengaluru, a flat is an "affordable residential apartment" for the 1% GST rate only if its carpet area is 60 sqm or less and the gross amount charged is ₹45 lakh or less. Gross amount includes land or undivided share, parking, preferential location and other promoter charges on top of the base price. Check with your CA.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is GST 1% on every flat under ₹45 lakh in Bengaluru?**: No. The flat must also have a carpet area of 60 sqm or less, because Bengaluru is a listed metropolitan city. The ₹45 lakh test is on the gross amount the promoter charges, which takes in land, parking and PLC as well as the base price.
- **Does parking count towards the ₹45 lakh limit?**: Yes, under the notification's definition. Gross amount includes any other amount the promoter charges the buyer, and parking charges are named in the text, along with preferential location, development and common facility charges.
- **Is the 60 sqm limit carpet area or super built-up area?**: Carpet area. The RERA Act defines carpet area as net usable floor area, excluding external walls, shafts, exclusive balconies and terraces. Sixty square metres is about 646 sq ft of carpet area.
- **Does the 90 sqm limit apply anywhere in Bengaluru?**: The 90 sqm limit is for cities and towns that are not metropolitan. Bengaluru is named as metropolitan, within its prescribed geographical limits. For a project near the city's edge, ask your CA which side of those limits it falls on.
- **Can an ongoing project still charge the old GST rates?**: Yes, if the promoter chose the old rates for that ongoing project by 10 May 2019 as the notification required. If it didn't, the new rates apply. Ask the promoter for proof of its choice.

## When must a builder hand over the apartment association and common areas in Karnataka?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/apartment-association-handover-karnataka/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** The RERA Act makes the builder help form an association of allottees and, after the occupancy certificate, hand common areas and documents to it. If local law is silent, the association is due within three months of a majority of units being booked, and conveyance within three months of the OC. Get the handover list in writing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **When must the association be formed under RERA?**: Section 11(4)(e) makes the promoter enable formation under the laws that apply. If there's no local law, it's due within three months of a majority of allottees having booked.
- **When must common areas be conveyed to the association?**: Within the period set by local law. If local law is silent, section 17(1) gives three months from the occupancy certificate.
- **Can the builder keep charging maintenance after the OC?**: Section 11(4)(d) makes the promoter provide essential services, on reasonable charges, until the association takes over maintenance. How long that runs in your project is a question for your lawyer and the association.
- **Do open parking areas go to the association?**: The Act lists open parking areas as common areas in section 2(n). Any exclusive rights given in individual agreements still need to be checked against that, so ask for a full parking inventory.
- **What if the builder never hands over the documents?**: Write formally, citing sections 11 and 17. If that fails, the association can authorise a Section 31 complaint to Karnataka RERA.

---

## How does an investment consultant assess builder track record in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/assess-builder-track-record-bangalore/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A careful real estate investment consultant looks at what the builder has actually delivered, not what it advertises. That means past projects' promised vs actual completion dates, whether occupancy certificates were issued, complaints and orders on the Karnataka RERA portal, build quality and upkeep in finished projects, how residents' associations were handed over, and any signs of financial strain.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **1. Delivery against promise**: For each of the builder's past projects in Bangalore, compare the completion date declared on the RERA portal (or the original agreement) with when residents actually got possession. One late project isn't a pattern. Several is.
- **2. Occupancy certificates**: Did past projects get their OC? A project where people moved in without one tells you something about how the builder handles approvals.
- **3. RERA complaints and orders**: The Karnataka RERA portal has complaint and order records. Search the builder's name and project names. Read a few orders. Look for patterns: delay, refunds, quality, handover. Our guide to checking a project on the Karnataka RERA website walks through each section.
- **4. Quality in finished projects**: Visit an older project by the same builder. Look at common areas, lifts, seepage, paint, landscaping. Talk to the security staff and a few residents if they're willing.
- **5. Handover to the association**: Section 17 of the RERA Act expects the promoter to hand over common areas to the association of allottees. Ask residents of older projects whether that happened smoothly, and whether maintenance funds were handed over.
- **Can I trust online builder reviews?**: Use them as a hint, not proof. Look for detailed, specific reviews and check them against RERA records.
- **Is a big-name builder always safer?**: Often more resourced, but big names have delayed projects too. Check the record project by project.
- **What if the builder is new?**: Look at the promoters' background, the project's approvals and its finances. Weigh the higher uncertainty against any price advantage.
- **Where are RERA complaints listed?**: On the Karnataka RERA portal, under complaints or orders. The format may change, so search by project and promoter name.
- **How far back should I look?**: The last several completed projects in Bangalore give a fair picture.

## How can I check a project on the Karnataka RERA website before buying?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/check-project-karnataka-rera-website/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Go to rera.karnataka.gov.in, use the project search to find the project by name or promoter, and open its registration details. Check that the registration is valid, the promoter and land match your documents, the approvals and sanctioned plans cover the tower and phase you're buying in, the declared completion date suits you, and there are no worrying complaints.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does every project need RERA registration?**: Not every one. The Act has exemptions, for example some small projects below set thresholds. Most large apartment projects in Bangalore need it. Ask your lawyer if a project claims an exemption.
- **What if the portal is slow or down?**: Try again later. Don't let a developer use that as a reason to skip the check.
- **Is RERA registration a guarantee the project is safe?**: No. It means the promoter has disclosed information and is subject to the Act. Title and quality still need checking.
- **Can I see the agreement for sale on the portal?**: The proforma agreement is part of the registration filing. Compare your draft with it. See checking the sale agreement before signing.
- **What do I do if details don't match?**: Ask the promoter in writing and tell your lawyer before paying anything.
- **How often should the project page change?**: Section 11(1) asks for quarterly updates on bookings, approvals and project status, so a page that hasn't changed in a year deserves a question.

---

## Construction-linked vs time-linked payment plan: which is safer?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/construction-linked-vs-time-linked-payment-plan/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** For most buyers, a construction-linked plan is safer, because you pay as the building actually goes up, so your money tracks real progress. A time-linked plan asks you to pay on fixed dates, whether or not construction has kept pace, which can leave you having paid a lot for a building that's behind.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a construction-linked plan always better?**: Usually safer. Not always cheaper. Weigh the price difference against the risk.
- **Can I switch plans after booking?**: Rarely, and only if the builder agrees. Decide before you sign.
- **What is a subvention scheme?**: The builder pays your loan interest for a period, often until possession. Read the terms carefully; if the builder stops paying, the bank may still look to you.
- **How do I verify construction progress?**: Visit the site, check the RERA quarterly updates (see how to read a quarterly RERA update), and ask for the architect's certificate for each stage.
- **Does the payment plan affect GST?**: GST depends on whether the price is paid before or after the completion certificate or first occupation. More in under-construction vs ready-to-move flats.
- **How much can a builder take before the agreement for sale?**: No more than 10% of the cost as an advance or application fee, under section 13(1). Anything beyond that needs a registered agreement for sale first.

---

## What documents should be verified before paying a token advance for a flat in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/documents-verify-before-token-advance-bangalore/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Before any token, check the project's Karnataka RERA registration and what the promoter filed there (approvals, commencement certificate, sanctioned plan, title declaration). Then check the title chain, Encumbrance Certificate, khata, land conversion where relevant, the draft agreement and the cost sheet. A consultant can gather these; a lawyer should give the title opinion.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How much token is normal for a Bangalore flat?**: It varies by developer and project. What's fixed by law is that a promoter can't take more than 10% of the unit cost as an advance without a written, registered agreement for sale (RERA section 13(1)).
- **Is a token refundable if my documents check fails?**: Only if the developer's terms say so. That's why you should read the refund conditions on the booking form before paying, not after.
- **Can I check these documents myself without a lawyer?**: You can do the RERA portal check, the cost sheet and the booking form yourself. Title and the agreement need a property lawyer.
- **Which document do buyers most often skip?**: The draft agreement for sale. People sign it weeks after the token, when they're already committed. Ask for the draft before you pay anything.
- **Does the RERA portal show everything I need?**: It shows what the promoter has filed, which is a lot. It isn't a title opinion and doesn't replace checking the original documents with a lawyer.

## How do I file a complaint with Karnataka RERA?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/file-complaint-karnataka-rera-online/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Any aggrieved person, including an allottees' association, can complain to Karnataka RERA under Section 31 of the RERA Act. K-RERA's FAQ says complaints go in Form 'N' with a ₹1,000 fee. Compensation claims under Sections 12, 14, 18 and 19 go to an adjudicating officer, not the Authority. The Authority aims to decide within 60 days.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Do I need a lawyer to file a RERA complaint in Karnataka?**: The Act doesn't require one. Many buyers still use a lawyer to frame the relief and choose between the Authority and the adjudicating officer, because filing in the wrong forum wastes months.
- **How much does it cost to file a complaint with K-RERA?**: K-RERA's FAQ states a ₹1,000 fee for a Form 'N' complaint to the Authority, and ₹5,000 for an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal. Lawyer's fees, if you hire one, are separate.
- **Can our apartment association file one complaint for everyone?**: Yes. Section 31's explanation says "person" includes an association of allottees. Bring the association's registration document and a resolution authorising the complaint.
- **Where do I claim compensation for delay?**: Compensation under Sections 12, 14, 18 and 19 is decided by an adjudicating officer appointed under Section 71, not through the Authority's general complaint route.
- **How do I track my hearing?**: K-RERA publishes daily cause lists on its website. Note your complaint number and check the list before each date.

---

## Villa vs apartment in East Bengaluru: what actually changes?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/gated-villa-vs-apartment-east-bengaluru/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** In the villa vs apartment choice, the real difference is what the deed gives you. An apartment gives you a unit plus an undivided share of the land. A villa may give you a marked plot, or just a bigger undivided share. Check that first, then compare land per rupee, upkeep per home and approvals.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a villa the same as an apartment under RERA?**: Yes, for registration. RERA's definition of apartment covers any self-contained unit "by any other name", so villa projects must register unless they fall under the 500 sq m or eight-unit exemption.
- **Do I own the land under a villa?**: Only if the deed gives you a marked plot with boundaries. Many villa projects sell an undivided share of the whole site instead, which works like a flat's share.
- **Is maintenance higher for a villa?**: Often, per home, because fewer homes split the common costs. In our illustrative example, ₹6 lakh a month split across 60 villas is ₹10,000 each, against ₹2,000 across 300 flats.
- **Does a villa hold value better than a flat?**: It can if you own a real plot, because land doesn't wear out the way a building does. That depends on the location and title, so check the deed and resale demand nearby.
- **What approvals should a villa have?**: Land conversion, layout approval for plotted projects, a building plan, a commencement certificate, RERA registration where required and an occupancy certificate for each villa.
- **What is the ROOF check?**: It's our four-part comparison: rights in the deed, obligations for approvals and repairs, real annual outgoings, and future options to rebuild, extend or sell.

---

## How do you gift a flat to a family member in Karnataka?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/gift-deed-flat-family-karnataka/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Gift deed stamp duty Karnataka charges for close family is fixed: ₹5,000 within BMRDA, BBMP or city corporation limits, ₹3,000 in municipal council or town panchayat areas, and ₹1,000 elsewhere, plus cess, surcharge and a registration fee. Gifts outside the family list pay the same duty as a sale. You register the deed on Kaveri.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What is the stamp duty on a gift deed in Karnataka?**: For a gift to a family member, fixed duty of ₹5,000 within BMRDA, BBMP or city corporation limits, ₹3,000 in municipal council or town panchayat areas, and ₹1,000 elsewhere, plus cess, surcharge and a registration fee. For anyone else, the same duty as a sale on the market value.
- **Who is a family member for a gift deed in Karnataka?**: Under Article 28 of the Karnataka Stamp Act: father, mother, husband, wife, son, daughter, daughter-in-law, brothers, sisters and grandchildren. Son-in-law, nephews, nieces, cousins, uncles and aunts aren't included.
- **How much does it cost to gift a flat to my son in Bengaluru?**: Inside GBA, about ₹6,600 in our example: ₹5,000 stamp duty, ₹500 cess, ₹100 surcharge and a registration fee that guides put at ₹1,000. Kaveri calculates the exact amount when you file.
- **Does a gift deed have to be registered?**: Yes. Under section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift of immovable property must be made by a registered instrument signed by the donor and attested by at least two witnesses. The donee must accept the gift during the donor's lifetime.
- **Can I gift a flat that still has a home loan?**: Talk to the lender first. The bank holds a charge on the flat, and a transfer usually needs its consent or the loan closed. Your lawyer can advise on the options.
- **Is a gifted flat taxed in the donee's hands?**: Gifts from relatives, as income-tax law defines them, generally aren't taxed in the donee's hands. That definition isn't the same as the Stamp Act's family list, and later sale and rental income have their own rules. Ask a CA for your case.

---

## How much GST do I pay on a new flat, and when is it zero?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/gst-on-flat-purchase-rates/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** GST on an under-construction flat bought from a builder is usually 1% without input tax credit for an affordable house and 5% without input tax credit for others, under the GST Council's 34th-meeting decisions. If the entire price is paid after the completion certificate or first occupation, whichever is earlier, this GST does not apply. Check invoices with a CA.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is GST 5% on every under-construction flat?**: No. An affordable house that meets the GST Council test is taxed at 1% without input tax credit. Other houses on the new rates pay 5% without input tax credit. Some ongoing projects took a one-time option to stay on the old 8% or 12% rates with credit.
- **When is GST on a new flat zero?**: When the entire consideration is received after the completion certificate, where required, or after first occupation, whichever is earlier. That is the exception in the construction-service rate entry. Check your payment dates and invoices with a CA. A "ready" label in a brochure is not enough.
- **Does the ₹45 lakh affordable cap include parking and PLC?**: The PIB note only says value up to ₹45 lakh. Which cost-sheet lines count towards that value is set by the notification, so have your CA map your cost sheet against it before you accept the 1% rate.
- **Is GST the same as stamp duty?**: No. GST, where it applies, is a tax on the construction service. Stamp duty and registration fees are state charges on the conveyance. An under-construction purchase can carry both. A sale after the completion certificate, with the full price paid after it, usually carries only stamp duty and registration.
- **Do NRI buyers pay a different GST rate on a flat?**: No separate NRI rate appears in the GST Council note. The same construction GST rules apply. TDS and payment-account rules are separate questions; see how TDS works on a flat purchase and ask a CA for the full picture.

---

## Do I need home insurance for a new flat, and what does it cover?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-insurance-new-flat/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Home insurance for a flat is your choice, not a RERA requirement on buyers, but it fills gaps the builder's duties don't. IRDAI's standard home policy, Bharat Griha Raksha, covers your flat and its fittings, and optionally your contents, against fire, flood, earthquake, storm, riots and similar events. It does not pay for poor construction.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is home insurance compulsory for a flat in Bengaluru?**: The RERA Act puts insurance duties on the promoter under section 16, not on buyers. A lender may set its own condition, so check your sanction letter and loan agreement.
- **Does home insurance cover cracks or leaks in a new flat?**: Not when they come from defective design, workmanship or materials, or the normal settling of a new building. Those go to the builder under the five-year defect liability in section 14(3) of the RERA Act.
- **Can I insure a flat before the sale deed is registered?**: Yes. The standard wording allows Home Building cover if you are occupying your home as purchaser under an agreement of sale.
- **Does the standard policy cover burglary?**: Only theft within 7 days of, and caused by, an insured event such as a fire or riot. Ask the insurer whether it sells a separate add-on for burglary.
- **Can a tenant insure their belongings?**: Yes. The wording lets a tenant, lessee or licensee buy Home Contents cover, while the owner buys Home Building cover.

---

## What documents do you need to sell or buy an inherited flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/inherited-flat-sale-documents/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** The core inherited property sale documents are the death certificate, the will or proof of who the heirs are, the parent deed and title chain, and the khata in the heirs' names. Every heir must sign the sale or release their share by a registered deed. Probate is no longer mandatory, but buyers and banks may still ask.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is probate needed to sell an inherited flat in Bengaluru?**: Not by law any more. The Repealing and Amending Act 2025 removed Section 213, which made probate compulsory for some wills. Buyers' banks may still prefer a probated will, so ask early.
- **Can I sell an inherited flat if one sibling refuses to sign?**: You can sell only your own share, which most buyers won't want. The usual routes are a registered release deed, a family settlement, or a partition suit in court. Talk to a lawyer.
- **How do I get a legal heir certificate in Karnataka?**: According to the Bengaluru Urban district site, it's now issued only to the kin of deceased government servants. Others apply to the jurisdictional civil court for a succession certificate.
- **Does a release deed need to be registered?**: Yes. A release deed transfers an interest in immovable property, so it must be registered and stamped. An unregistered letter, affidavit or NOC doesn't transfer a share.
- **How are shares split if there's no will?**: For a Hindu man, Section 10 of the Hindu Succession Act gives one share each to the widow, each son, each daughter and his mother. Other communities follow their own personal laws.
- **What is the HEIRS check?**: It's our five-step plan for an inherited flat: list the heirs, gather evidence, take inventory of title papers, get releases or signatures, and make the khata sale-ready.

---

## Is GST charged on apartment maintenance in Bengaluru?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/maintenance-charges-gst-apartment/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** CBIC Circular No. 109/28/2019-GST clarifies that RWA maintenance contributions up to ₹7,500 per month per member can be exempt. GST applies only when that monthly contribution exceeds ₹7,500 and the RWA's annual aggregate turnover is ₹20 lakh or more. If the monthly amount exceeds the limit, the circular taxes the entire amount, not only the excess.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is maintenance always GST-free below ₹7,500?**: Under Circular 109, contributions up to ₹7,500 per month per member for common-use services can be exempt. Confirm your society's facts with a CA, especially if other taxable supplies exist.
- **What if my bill is ₹8,000 but the society's turnover is under ₹20 lakh?**: Circular 109 says that if aggregate turnover does not exceed ₹20 lakh, the RWA need not register and pay GST even when monthly charges exceed ₹7,500. Turnover is an association-level fact; ask the treasurer for the basis.
- **Is GST only on the amount above ₹7,500?**: CBIC Circular 109's example taxes the entire contribution once the ceiling is crossed. Some court discussions take a different view. Mark contested outcomes for CA advice; this page follows the circular's published example.
- **Does Bengaluru have a different rule from the rest of India?**: Not on the face of Circular 109. The circular is a CBIC clarification for RWAs generally. SGST still appears on taxable invoices in Karnataka in the normal way.
- **Are builder advance-maintenance invoices the same as RWA invoices?**: Not necessarily. Promoter billing before handover can differ from association billing after takeover. Keep both paper trails and have a CA read any large GST line before possession payment.

## New launch or resale flat in the same area: what changes for me?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/new-launch-vs-resale-flat-what-changes/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A new launch is bought from a promoter, so the RERA Act's promoter duties, the 10% advance cap and construction GST come into play. A resale flat is bought from an owner, so title history, the OC, khata and the seller's paperwork carry more weight. Compare the risks as well as the price per square foot.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does RERA apply when I buy a resale flat?**: RERA governs promoters and real estate projects. The Act's definition of "allottee" includes a person who later acquires an allotment by sale or transfer, so some protections may reach a resale buyer in a registered project. Ask your lawyer how that applies to your flat.
- **Is GST charged on a resale flat?**: The construction GST entry excludes cases where the entire consideration is received after the completion certificate or first occupation, whichever is earlier. A sale by an owner of a completed flat usually falls outside it, but confirm with your CA.
- **Can the seller of a resale flat take any amount as token?**: Section 13(1)'s 10% cap applies to promoters, not to individual sellers. Agree the token and the refund terms in writing and have your lawyer check them first.
- **Who fixes defects in a five-year-old resale flat?**: Section 14(3) runs five years from the date possession was first handed over. After that, repairs usually fall on the owner or the association. Get an engineer's inspection before you buy.
- **Do I pay TDS on both new and resale flats?**: Yes, once the deal crosses the threshold. If the seller is an NRI, different TDS rules apply. Check with your CA.

## Does a housing society nomination replace a will?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/nomination-vs-will-flat/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** No. In the nomination vs will property question, the will decides who owns your flat; a nomination only tells a society, association or bank whom to deal with after your death. The Supreme Court has held that a nominee isn't the owner and heirs keep their rights. To leave the flat to someone specific, write a valid will.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does a nominee become the owner of a flat?**: Not by being a nominee. The Supreme Court held in 2016 that a society's transfer to a nominee has no bearing on title between heirs, and in 2023 that nomination doesn't override succession law.
- **Which wins, the will or the nomination?**: The will, if it's valid. A nominee who isn't the beneficiary under the will holds things for the people entitled to them under the will or succession law.
- **Do I need to register my will in Karnataka?**: No. Registering a will is optional under the Registration Act 1908. It does make the will harder to challenge and easier to locate later.
- **How many witnesses does a will need?**: At least two, under Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act. Each must see you sign or hear you acknowledge your signature, and sign in your presence.
- **If a flat is jointly owned, does the survivor get it all?**: Not automatically. Only the deceased's share passes, by will or succession. In our example, a widow ends up with 66.67% and each child with 16.67%.
- **What is the KEEP check?**: It's our four-step plan: know your heirs, execute a valid will, enter matching nominations everywhere, and place the papers where your executor can find them.

---

## What does an NRI need to buy a flat in East Bangalore without travelling?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-us-buy-bangalore-without-travel-poa/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** You need four things: money routed through Indian banking channels (inward remittance or an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO account), a trusted person in India holding your power of attorney, a Bangalore consultant who can run video visits and handle documents, and your own lawyer and CA. NRIs can buy flats, but not agricultural land or farmhouses.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can an NRI buy a flat in Bangalore without ever visiting?**: Yes, it's commonly done with a power of attorney holder in India handling registration and possession, and a consultant and lawyer handling the rest. You'll still need to sign and execute the PoA properly where you live.
- **Can OCI card holders buy flats in Bangalore?**: Yes. Under RBI's FEMA rules, OCIs can buy residential property in India other than agricultural land, plantation property or farm houses, on the same payment terms as NRIs.
- **Can I pay for the flat from my foreign bank account directly?**: Payment has to reach India through banking channels as an inward remittance, or come from your NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO account. Talk to your bank about the cleanest route for your situation.
- **Do I need a PAN to buy property in India as an NRI?**: For practical purposes, yes. You'll need it for TDS filing, registration and any home loan. Apply early, because it can take time.
- **Is it risky to give my parents power of attorney?**: The risk is less about who and more about scope. A PoA limited to one unit and specific acts is much safer than a general one. Have your lawyer draft it.

---

## Can OCI cardholders buy flats in Bengaluru?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/oci-buy-property-india-rules/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes. The OCI property purchase India rules under FEMA match an NRI's: you can buy flats, houses, plots and commercial property without RBI approval, but not farmland, farmhouses or plantations. Pay through Indian banking channels or NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO accounts. A 2021 Supreme Court ruling didn't change this, the RBI says.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Do OCI cardholders need RBI permission to buy a flat?**: No. Under Rule 24 of the FEMA Non-Debt Instruments Rules 2019, OCIs can buy residential and commercial property without RBI approval. The RBI confirmed this in a December 2021 clarification.
- **Can an OCI buy agricultural land in Karnataka?**: No. OCIs can't buy agricultural land, farmhouses or plantations. They can inherit them, and can sell or gift them only to a person resident in India.
- **How many properties can an OCI buy?**: There's no limit on the number under FEMA. Repatriating sale proceeds on the property route is limited to two residential properties, so plan which ones you fund in foreign exchange.
- **Can an OCI get a home loan in India?**: Yes. FEMA's Borrowing and Lending Regulations let banks, NBFCs and housing finance companies lend to OCIs for a home, with RBI's usual loan-to-value caps. Each lender sets its own documents.
- **Can my foreign spouse buy with me?**: A spouse who isn't an NRI or OCI can buy one property jointly with an NRI or OCI spouse, subject to the conditions in Rule 25. Check them with a lawyer before you book.
- **What is the CARD check?**: It's our four-point check for OCI buyers: confirm the property category, choose the payment account, check the relatives rule for gifts, and get your documents ready.

---

## Why does one project have several RERA registration numbers?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/phase-wise-rera-registration/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Because RERA treats each phase as its own project. The Explanation to section 3 says that where a project is developed in phases, every phase is a stand-alone real estate project needing separate registration. So a large township can carry several RERA numbers, each with its own completion date, approvals and quarterly updates.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it normal for one project to have several RERA numbers?**: Yes. The Explanation to section 3 requires each phase to be registered separately as a stand-alone project, so a multi-phase project carries several numbers.
- **Which RERA number should be on my agreement?**: The registration number of the phase that includes your tower and unit. Check it matches the allotment letter and the portal listing.
- **Do different phases have different completion dates?**: They can. Each registration is valid for the completion period declared for that phase under section 4(2)(l)(C).
- **Can amenities sit in a different phase from my flat?**: Yes. Ask which registration covers the clubhouse and other shared areas, and check that phase's completion date and plans.
- **Can a builder take bookings for a phase that isn't registered yet?**: No. Section 3 bars advertising, marketing, booking or selling any part of a project that requires registration before it's registered.

---

## Can I claim home loan interest paid before possession?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/pre-construction-interest-deduction/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes, but not in the years you paid it. Section 22(1)(c) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 lets interest for the period before the tax year in which the home is acquired or constructed be claimed in five equal instalments, starting that year. For a self-occupied home, caps and your tax regime decide how much you actually get.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I claim home loan interest during construction every year?**: No. Under section 22(1)(c) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, interest for the period before the tax year in which the property is acquired or constructed is claimed in five equal instalments, starting that year, not in the years it was paid.
- **What is the limit on home loan interest for a self-occupied house?**: Section 22(2) caps the clause (b) interest deduction at ₹2,00,000 for self-occupied houses if construction is completed within five years and you have the lender's certificate, and at ₹30,000 otherwise. The total for such houses can't exceed ₹2,00,000.
- **What happens if my builder delays beyond five years?**: The ₹2,00,000 cap applies only if acquisition or construction is completed within five years from the end of the tax year in which the loan was taken. After that, the cap for a self-occupied home falls to ₹30,000.
- **Can I claim home loan interest under the new tax regime?**: For a self-occupied home, section 202 computes income without the section 22(1)(b) interest deduction. The list doesn't name clause (c), so ask your CA how your pre-construction instalments are treated under the regime you choose.
- **Does possession date decide when the five instalments start?**: The Act uses the tax year in which the property is acquired or constructed, not the word possession. Your CA should fix that year using your OC, possession letter and sale deed.

---

## Is it safe to pay an EOI for a pre-launch project in Bangalore before RERA registration?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/pre-launch-projects-bangalore-risk/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** It's risky, and a real estate investment consultant shouldn't push you into it. Section 3 of the RERA Act says a promoter can't advertise, market, book, sell or offer for sale any unit in a project that needs registration until it's registered.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a refundable EOI safe?**: Safer than a non-refundable one, but only as good as the developer's willingness to pay. Get the terms in writing.
- **Can a consultant take EOIs?**: Section 10(a) bars a registered agent from facilitating sales in an unregistered project. Be cautious with any consultant collecting EOIs.
- **Will I miss out if I wait for RERA registration?**: Maybe on the earliest price. You gain the ability to check what you're buying. Many buyers think that's worth it.
- **What if the developer is well known?**: A big name reduces some risk, but not the legal position. Plans can still change before registration. See builder track record.
- **Where do I complain about a pre-launch scheme?**: Karnataka RERA handles complaints on registered projects and agents. See how to file a complaint with Karnataka RERA. For unregistered-project issues, talk to a lawyer about consumer and other remedies.
- **What if the developer says registration is "applied for"?**: An application isn't a registration. Section 3 turns on the project being registered, so wait for the registration number on rera.karnataka.gov.in before you pay.

## How much do real estate consultancy services cost in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/real-estate-consultancy-services-cost-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** On new projects in Bangalore, real estate consultancy services often cost the buyer nothing directly, because the developer pays the consultant. On resale, you may pay a brokerage. Some advisers charge a fixed fee instead. There's no single official rate, so ask each firm for its exact terms in writing before you start.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Do I pay brokerage on a new flat in Bangalore?**: Often not, when the consultant is paid by the developer. Confirm with the consultant and check your cost sheet.
- **What's a normal brokerage for resale in Bangalore?**: It's set by agreement, not law, and varies. Agree the figure in writing before visits start.
- **Do consultancy fees attract GST?**: Services provided for a fee may attract GST. Check the invoice and ask your CA.
- **Can I negotiate a consultant's fee?**: Yes, on fees you pay directly. Developer-side payments are between the consultant and the builder.
- **Is a paid adviser better than a free one?**: Not automatically. A paid adviser may have less sales bias, but quality still varies. Judge on disclosure and the checks they do. Also see what real estate consultancy services include.
- **Should the fee be in a contract?**: Yes. Get the fee, the scope of work and who else might pay them into a written agreement before you start.

## Rent vs buy in Bengaluru: how should you work it out?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rent-vs-buy-bengaluru/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** For rent vs buy in Bengaluru, compare a year's rent with a year's unrecoverable cost of owning: loan interest, maintenance, tax and the return your down payment could have earned. Add the one-time 7.6% stamp and registration charges. Buying wins if you'll stay long enough for price growth to cover the gap.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it better to rent or buy in Bengaluru?**: It depends on your numbers and how long you'll stay. Compare a year's rent with a year's loan interest, maintenance, tax and the return lost on your down payment, then add the one-time 7.6% charges. If you'll stay many years in an area with steady price growth, buying can win.
- **Should I compare my EMI with my rent?**: No. Part of every EMI repays principal, which you keep as equity. Compare rent with the costs you never get back: interest, maintenance, property tax, lost return on your cash, and the stamp and registration charges.
- **What is the rent yield in Bengaluru?**: It varies by flat and area, and we don't have an official citywide figure. Work it out yourself: annual rent divided by the price. A ₹35,000 monthly rent on a ₹1 crore flat is a 4.2% gross yield, below a typical home loan rate.
- **How much price growth does buying need to beat renting?**: In our example, about 4.5% a year just to cover the year-one gap between owning costs and rent, plus enough to recover 7.6% in one-time charges. Over five years that came to roughly 30% in total. Your own figures will differ.
- **Does the tax benefit on a home loan change the answer?**: It can narrow the gap if you're in the old tax regime and claim interest and principal deductions. Under the default new regime, those deductions for a self-occupied home generally aren't available. Ask a CA to run it for your income before relying on it.
- **How long should I stay to make buying worth it?**: Long enough for price growth to recover the one-time charges and the yearly gap. In our example, five years needed about 5.4% growth a year. Shorter stays usually favour renting on numbers alone.

---

## Renting out a flat in Karnataka: agreement, stamp duty and police check

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rental-agreement-new-owner-karnataka/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under rental agreement Karnataka rules, a home let for up to a year pays stamp duty of 0.5% on the rent and deposit, capped at ₹500. Longer leases pay 1% with no cap and must be registered. Tell the local police station about your tenant; the state's online tenant service was listed as under modification on 19 Oct 2026.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What is the stamp duty on a rental agreement in Karnataka?**: For a home let for up to a year, 0.5% of the rent and deposit, capped at ₹500. For one to ten years, 1% of the average annual rent plus deposit, with no cap. Longer terms pay more. Leases to close family pay a fixed ₹5,000, ₹3,000 or ₹1,000 by location.
- **Is registration of a rental agreement compulsory in Karnataka?**: It's compulsory for leases from year to year, for more than a year, or reserving a yearly rent, under section 17(1)(d) of the Registration Act. That's why 11-month agreements are common. You can still register a shorter one.
- **Does the security deposit count for stamp duty?**: Yes. Article 30 counts "money advanced", which includes the security deposit whether it's refundable or adjusted against rent. Add it to the rent before working out the duty.
- **Why are rental agreements usually 11 months?**: Because leases over a year must be registered and pay 1% duty with no cap, while a residential agreement up to a year pays at most ₹500 and needn't be registered. An 11-month term keeps it simple, at the cost of renewing more often.
- **How do I do tenant police verification in Bengaluru?**: The official online tenant verification listing showed "Service Under Modification" on 19 Oct 2026. Submit the tenant information form at the police station covering your flat, with the tenant's ID, address proof and photos, and keep the acknowledgement.
- **Do I pay tax on rent from my flat?**: Rent is taxable income, and some tenants paying high rent must deduct TDS. The rules changed with the Income-tax Act 2025, so ask a CA how they apply to you.

---

## My project&#x27;s RERA date was extended. What does it mean for me?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-extension-what-it-means-buyer/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Section 6 lets the Authority extend a project's registration for force majeure, or in reasonable circumstances without promoter default, with written reasons, capped at one year in aggregate. An approved extension moves the registration end date. It does not by itself rewrite your agreement possession date or cancel section 18 delay rights.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can Karnataka RERA extend a project by more than one year?**: The first proviso caps extension on "reasonable circumstances" grounds at one year in aggregate. Anything beyond that is outside the plain wording of that proviso. Confirm what your project's order actually grants and on which ground.
- **Is every COVID-related delay automatically force majeure under section 6?**: No. Force majeure for section 6 is defined in the Explanation. Whether a past pandemic-related order fits that definition, or the separate "reasonable circumstances" limb in the first proviso, is for the Authority's recorded reasons and your lawyer's reading, not a sales email.
- **My agreement date has passed but RERA shows a later date. Which one counts for delay interest?**: Section 18 looks at the agreement for sale (and at suspension/revocation cases). The RERA registration end date is a different clock. Your lawyer applies both to your facts.
- **Do I have to consent to an extension?**: Section 6 is an application by the promoter to the Authority, not a two-thirds allottee vote (unlike certain plan changes under section 14). You can still object through representations or a complaint if the extension or the underlying delay harms you; strategy is case-specific.
- **Does an extension mean the builder is not in default?**: The proviso allows extension only in force majeure or in reasonable circumstances without promoter default, with written reasons. That is a finding for registration purposes. It is not the same document as a court or Authority order deciding your individual section 18 claim.

---

## How do I read a project&#x27;s quarterly progress report on Karnataka RERA?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-quarterly-progress-report-how-to-read/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Open the project on rera.karnataka.gov.in and look at four things the promoter must update every quarter: units booked, garages booked, approvals taken and pending, and construction status with photographs. Then check the dates. A page that hasn't moved in several quarters is a question to put to the builder in writing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How often must a builder update the Karnataka RERA project page?**: Every quarter. Section 11(1) of the RERA Act requires quarterly updates on bookings, garages, approvals and project status. The Karnataka Rules FAQs say these must be uploaded within fifteen days from the end of each quarter.
- **Do quarterly updates include construction photographs?**: Yes. The K-RERA FAQs list construction status of each building, each floor, and internal infrastructure and common areas, each with photographs.
- **Can I rely only on the quarterly update instead of a site visit?**: No. The update is what the promoter has declared. Use it to prepare questions, then visit the site and check your tower yourself.
- **What if the builder's payment demand doesn't match the RERA progress update?**: Ask the builder in writing to explain the gap before you pay, and share both documents with your lawyer. If you have a home loan, raise the gap with your lender before the next tranche is released.
- **Is missing a quarterly update a RERA violation?**: Section 11(1) makes the updates a duty of the promoter, and section 61 provides a penalty for contravening the Act. Whether to complain in a particular case is something to decide with your lawyer.

---

## What happens if my project&#x27;s RERA registration has lapsed?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-registration-lapsed-project/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A RERA registration is valid only for the completion period the builder declared, plus any section 6 extension (capped at one year in aggregate for reasons other than force majeure). If it lapses or is revoked, section 8 lets the Authority, after consulting the appropriate Government, arrange the remaining work, including through the association of allottees. Section 18 protects you.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a lapsed RERA registration the same as a cancelled project?**: No. Lapse means the validity period ended without completion or extension. The Act doesn't cancel your agreement on lapse, and the Authority can act under section 8.
- **How long can RERA registration be extended?**: Section 6 allows extension for force majeure, and separately, without promoter default, for reasons recorded in writing, not exceeding one year in aggregate.
- **Who completes a project after its registration is revoked?**: The Authority decides under section 8, after consulting the appropriate Government. The association of allottees has the first right of refusal to carry out the remaining work.
- **Can I get a refund if the registration is revoked?**: Section 19(4) gives allottees a right to refund with interest and compensation if the promoter can't give possession because its registration is suspended or revoked. Take legal advice on your case.
- **Should I stop paying instalments if the registration lapsed?**: Not without legal advice. Section 19(6) still requires you to pay as the agreement says, and section 19(7) charges interest on delay. Use the Act's remedies instead.

---

## What should I check on a site visit to an under-construction project?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/site-visit-checklist-under-construction/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Open the project's Karnataka RERA page before you go. At the site, match the RERA number on the board, ask to see the sanctioned plans, compare the build stage with the builder's last quarterly update, and treat the sample flat as a sales tool. Write down what the sales team says and get key answers in writing before paying.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can the builder refuse to show me the sanctioned plans?**: Section 11(3)(a) of the RERA Act makes the promoter responsible for making the sanctioned plans, layout plans and specifications available at booking, by display at the site or wherever the regulations specify. Section 19(1) gives allottees the right to that information. If you're refused, note it and raise it in writing.
- **Is the sample flat what I'll actually get?**: Not necessarily. The agreement for sale and the approved specifications decide what you get. Photograph the sample flat and ask which items are display only. Section 12 gives you a remedy if you paid on the basis of a model apartment that turned out to be false or incorrect.
- **How can I tell if construction is on schedule?**: Compare the build stage you see with the latest quarterly update on the project's Karnataka RERA page and the completion date the builder declared. A site visit can't confirm the schedule on its own, but a big gap is a fair question to put to the builder in writing.
- **Should I pay a token amount during the site visit?**: Not before you've checked the RERA page, read the draft agreement, and had your lawyer review title and approvals. Section 13(1) caps the advance before a registered agreement for sale at 10% of the cost.
- **What should I carry on a site visit?**: Your phone with the RERA page open, a notebook or notes app, a measuring tape if you want to check the sample flat, and a list of questions. Wear closed shoes if you'll walk the construction area.

---

## Do women get a stamp duty concession in Karnataka?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/stamp-duty-women-buyers-karnataka/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** On stamp duty for female in Karnataka, the rates are the same as for men. The Stamp Act's conveyance rates don't vary by the buyer's gender, and we found no notification giving women a concession as of 19 Oct 2026. A flat above ₹45 lakh in Bengaluru costs about 7.6% in charges whoever's name is on the deed.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is stamp duty lower for women in Karnataka?**: No. The Karnataka Stamp Act's conveyance rates don't vary by gender, and we found no notification giving women a concession as of 19 Oct 2026. A woman buying a flat above ₹45 lakh in Bengaluru pays the same 5% duty, cess, surcharge and 2% registration fee as anyone else.
- **Does registering a flat in my wife's name save stamp duty?**: No. On an ₹80 lakh resale flat in GBA, the charges come to ₹6,08,000 whether the deed names a woman, a man or both. Choose names for control, inheritance and loan reasons, not to save duty.
- **Is the registration fee different for women?**: No. The registration fee went from 1% to 2% on 31 Aug 2025 under a Revenue Department notification, with no distinction by gender.
- **What is the stamp duty on a gift from husband to wife in Karnataka?**: Under Article 28(b) of the Karnataka Stamp Act, a gift to a family member, including a spouse, carries fixed duty: ₹5,000 within BMRDA, BBMP or city corporation limits, ₹3,000 in municipal council or town panchayat areas, and ₹1,000 elsewhere, plus cess, surcharge and the registration fee.
- **Could Karnataka introduce a women's concession?**: It could. The government can grant remissions by notification. None applied as of 19 Oct 2026 that we could find, so don't build one into your budget. Confirm with the sub-registrar office before registration.
- **Do joint owners pay stamp duty twice?**: No. Duty is charged once on the deed, on the higher of the price and the guidance value, however many buyers are named.

## Does RERA require title insurance, and does it protect me?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/title-insurance-rera/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Section 16 of the RERA Act requires the builder to obtain the insurances the appropriate Government notifies, including on the title of the land and building and on construction. The builder pays the premium, and the benefit passes to you when the agreement for sale is signed. It applies only once notified, and it doesn't replace your own title check.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does RERA require builders to take title insurance?**: Section 16(1) requires the promoter to obtain the insurances notified by the appropriate Government, including on title of the land and building. The duty applies only once the cover is notified, so whether it applies to a Karnataka project is a point to confirm with your lawyer.
- **Who pays the title insurance premium under RERA?**: The promoter. Section 16(2) makes the promoter liable for premium and charges, payable before the insurance is transferred to the association.
- **When does title insurance transfer to the buyer?**: Under section 16(3), at the time the promoter enters into the agreement for sale with the allottee. The documents go to the association once it's formed.
- **If there's title insurance, do I still need a lawyer?**: Yes. Insurance pays on a covered loss; it doesn't cure a defective title. Your own lawyer's title search remains essential.
- **What if the title turns out to be defective?**: Section 18(2) makes the promoter compensate you for loss due to defective title of the land, and the claim isn't time-barred under other laws. Take legal advice on your case.

## Can a real estate consultancy compare under-construction and ready-to-move flats for me?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/under-construction-vs-ready-to-move-consultancy/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes, and it's one of the more useful things real estate consultancy services can do. A side-by-side comparison should cover total cost, delay risk, GST, loan interest during construction, what you can inspect, the paperwork, and when you can actually live there or rent it out. The right answer depends on your timeline and how much risk you can carry.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is under-construction always cheaper?**: Usually on base price, not always on total cost once you add GST, rent and pre-EMI.
- **What if my under-construction flat is delayed?**: Section 18 of the RERA Act gives you remedies.
- **Can a flat be "ready" without an OC?**: Some are sold that way. That's a risk for khata, loans and utilities. Ask your lawyer.
- **Do banks lend on both?**: Yes, subject to their checks. Under-construction loans are disbursed in stages. See how under-construction home-loan tranches and pre-EMI work.
- **What about "nearly ready" flats?**: Ask whether the completion certificate has been issued and when you'll pay the balance. That affects GST. Also see payment plans.
- **Can a builder extend the completion date on its own?**: No. Extending a project's registration needs the Authority's approval under section 6, which covers force majeure and, where the promoter isn't at fault, up to one year in aggregate. Your agreement's date still governs your section 18 rights.
