## What is undivided share (UDS) of land, and why should a flat buyer care?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/undivided-share-uds-explained/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Undivided share is your proportionate interest in the land and other common areas of the project, held together with every other owner and never split off as a separate piece. Under RERA, the builder must convey that proportionate title in the common areas to the association, so check how your agreement and sale deed state it.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I sell my undivided share of land separately from my flat?**: The K-RERA proforma agreement says the share in the common areas "is undivided and cannot be divided or separated". Ask your lawyer how your own deed treats it.
- **Does a higher UDS mean I own a bigger plot?**: No. UDS is a proportionate interest in the whole land and common areas, shared with all owners, not a separate plot you can mark out.
- **Is UDS the same as carpet area?**: No. Carpet area under section 2(k) is the usable floor area inside your flat. UDS is your proportionate share of the land and common areas outside it.
- **Who gets title to the common areas under RERA?**: Sections 11(4)(f) and 17(1) require the promoter to convey the undivided proportionate title in the common areas to the association of allottees or the competent authority.
- **Where is UDS written in my documents?**: Usually in the apartment schedule of the agreement for sale and in the sale deed. The K-RERA proforma has a separate column for undivided share.

---

# Category: Agreements, Contracts & Possession

## Allotment letter, agreement for sale, sale deed: what is the difference?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/allotment-letter-vs-agreement-vs-sale-deed/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** An allotment letter is usually an early booking paper. The agreement for sale is the registered contract that fixes price, specifications and the possession date under RERA. The sale deed (conveyance) transfers title to you. Under section 13, a builder can't take more than 10% of the cost before that agreement is written and registered.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is an allotment letter enough to pay 20% of the flat cost?**: Under section 13(1), a promoter must not take more than 10% as advance or application fee without a written, registered agreement for sale. Paying more on an allotment letter alone is a red flag, so speak to your lawyer first.
- **Does the agreement for sale transfer ownership?**: No. It's the contract that governs the purchase. Ownership passes on the registered conveyance (sale) deed under section 17.
- **Must the agreement for sale be registered?**: Section 13(1) requires the agreement for sale to be entered into and registered under the law in force before the promoter can take more than 10% as advance.
- **Can the builder cancel my allotment?**: Section 11(5) allows cancellation only on the terms of the agreement for sale. Unilateral cancellation without sufficient cause can be taken to the Authority.
- **What should I bring to my lawyer at booking?**: The allotment letter, payment receipts, RERA registration number, draft agreement for sale, and the brochure specifications you were shown.

---

## Which booking form clauses should I check before paying for a flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/booking-form-clauses-red-flags/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Check how much the form asks you to pay, what happens to that money if you or the builder back out, and whether it binds you to terms you haven't seen. Under section 13 of the RERA Act, a promoter can't take more than 10% of the cost as an advance or application fee before a registered agreement for sale.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How much can a builder take at booking under RERA?**: Section 13(1) of the RERA Act caps advance payments or application fees at 10% of the cost of the apartment until a written agreement for sale is signed and registered.
- **Is a booking form legally binding?**: It can create obligations about the booking amount, so treat it as a contract. The detailed terms of the purchase belong in the agreement for sale under section 13(2). Have your lawyer read both.
- **Can the builder keep my whole booking amount if I cancel?**: That depends on the form and the agreement, and on whether the deduction is fair on your facts. Section 11(5) lets you approach the Authority if the builder cancels your allotment unilaterally, without sufficient cause and outside the agreement's terms. Ask your lawyer before you accept a forfeiture.
- **Should I sign a booking form without seeing the agreement for sale?**: It's safer not to. Ask for the draft agreement first so you know the payment plan, possession date and default interest terms you are being asked to accept.
- **What if the builder asks for more than 10% before the agreement?**: Ask for the agreement to be executed and registered first. Section 13(1) bars the promoter from accepting more than 10% as advance or application fee without it.

---

## Can a builder change the plan after I book a flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/builder-changes-plan-after-booking/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Not freely. Under section 14(2) of the RERA Act, once plans and specifications are disclosed to you, the builder needs your prior consent to change your apartment, and the prior written consent of at least two-thirds of allottees to change the building or common areas. Only limited minor changes are exempt.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can a builder add a floor after I book?**: Not without the prior written consent of at least two-thirds of the allottees in that building under section 14(2)(ii). An addition to height or area is not a minor change.
- **Does a clause in my booking form allow the builder to change plans?**: Section 14(2) applies notwithstanding any contract or agreement, so a general discretion clause doesn't remove the consent requirement.
- **Can the builder change my flat's layout?**: Only with your previous consent, except for minor changes you request or minor non-structural changes certified by an architect or engineer and intimated to you.
- **How are allottees counted for the two-thirds rule?**: Each allottee counts once, however many flats they or their family have booked. Companies and their associated entities also count once, and the promoter is excluded.
- **Where do I complain if the plan was changed without consent?**: To Karnataka RERA under section 31. Keep the disclosed plans, your agreement and any notice of the change as evidence.

---

## What happens to my flat if the builder goes insolvent?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/builder-insolvency-homebuyer-rights/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** If the builder is a company or LLP, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code treats the money you paid as financial debt, which makes you a financial creditor. Buyers in the same project can start insolvency together, vote through an authorised representative, and share in any resolution plan. Pending cases against the builder pause during the moratorium.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Are homebuyers financial creditors under the IBC?**: Yes. The Explanation to section 5(8)(f) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code deems money raised from an allottee under a real estate project to have the commercial effect of a borrowing, so allottees are financial creditors.
- **How many flat buyers are needed to file insolvency against a builder?**: Under the second proviso to section 7(1), at least 100 allottees of the same real estate project or 10% of that project's allottees, whichever is less, must file jointly.
- **Can I continue my RERA complaint after the builder goes into insolvency?**: Section 14 bars the continuation of proceedings against the corporate debtor before any court, tribunal or other authority during the moratorium. Ask your lawyer how this applies to your RERA case.
- **Who votes for homebuyers in the committee of creditors?**: An insolvency professional appointed as authorised representative under section 21(6A)(b). Under section 25A(3A), they vote as more than 50% of the voting share of buyers who cast their vote decide.
- **How long does a builder's insolvency process take?**: Section 12 sets 180 days, extendable by the tribunal, with a mandatory limit of 330 days including extensions and time in legal proceedings.

---

## Can a builder in Bengaluru charge separately for car parking?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/can-builder-sell-car-parking-separately/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** The RERA Act treats "open parking areas" as common areas, which belong to all allottees. A "garage", meaning a roofed space walled on three sides, is defined separately and can be a distinct item. Whether a covered stilt or basement slot counts as one turns on its physical form and your agreement. Ask what you're paying for.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can a builder sell open parking in Bengaluru?**: Under the RERA Act, open parking areas are listed as common areas, which belong to all allottees. A charge labelled as a sale of an open slot is worth questioning. Ask what right you'd actually get.
- **Is a basement parking slot a "garage" under RERA?**: Only if it has a roof and walls on three sides. That's the Act's definition. Most painted basement bays don't meet it.
- **Should my parking slot be numbered in the agreement?**: Ask for that. A numbered, allotted slot shown on the plan gives you something specific to enforce if a dispute arises after handover.
- **Does parking count towards TDS and stamp duty?**: If the parking amount is part of the consideration for the transfer, it likely affects both. Confirm the treatment with a chartered accountant before you pay.
- **What happens to unsold parking at handover?**: Common areas, including open parking, are meant to pass to the association. Ask the builder in writing how unsold or visitor bays will be handed over.

---

## Can I cancel a flat booking and get my money back under RERA?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/cancel-flat-booking-refund-rera/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** It depends who cancelled and why. If the builder misses the agreement handover date, section 18 lets you withdraw for a refund with prescribed interest, or stay and claim delay interest. If you cancel for your own reasons, the Act gives no general exit right; your agreement and booking terms control deductions.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I cancel within a cooling-off period after booking?**: The RERA Act does not set a universal cooling-off window for flat bookings. Any short cancellation window, if it exists, comes from your booking form or agreement, not from a general Act clause.
- **If the builder cancels my allotment, do I automatically get a full refund?**: Not automatically. Section 11(5) lets you seek relief if the cancellation was not in terms of the agreement and was unilateral without sufficient cause. The refund amount still follows the agreement and any order the Authority passes.
- **Does paying only the booking amount make a refund easier?**: The amount at stake is smaller, but the written booking terms still decide what comes back. Section 13 also limits how much the promoter can take before a registered agreement exists.
- **Will delay interest continue if I stay in the project?**: Under the proviso to section 18(1), if you do not withdraw, the promoter must pay interest for every month of delay until possession, at the prescribed rate. Confirm calculation and start date with your lawyer.
- **Should I stop paying instalments when I decide to cancel?**: Stopping payment can put you in breach under section 19(6)–(7) while your exit is still unsettled. Take advice before you skip a demand.

---

## Carpet area vs super built-up area: what does RERA say a flat is?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/carpet-area-vs-super-built-up-rera/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under the RERA Act, carpet area is the flat's net usable floor area, including internal walls. It excludes external walls, service shafts, exclusive balconies and exclusive terraces. "Super built-up area" isn't defined in the Act at all. It's a sales figure that loads a share of lobbies, lifts and clubhouse onto your flat.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a balcony included in carpet area?**: Not if it's your exclusive balcony. The RERA definition excludes "exclusive balcony or verandah area". Builders usually list it as a separate figure, so check both numbers.
- **Is super built-up area legal to quote?**: The RERA Act doesn't define it. Your agreement and the RERA filing should give carpet area, so treat any super built-up figure as a sales number and convert to carpet before you compare.
- **What loading percentage is normal in Bengaluru?**: There's no legal standard, and we don't publish a "typical" figure. Work it out for each project from the builder's own carpet and super built-up numbers.
- **Are internal walls part of carpet area?**: Yes. The Act's definition specifically includes "the area covered by the internal partition walls of the apartment". External walls are excluded.
- **Should I measure the flat at possession?**: Yes. Measure room by room using the RERA definition and compare it with the carpet area in your agreement. Raise any shortfall with the builder in writing first.

---

## What should I check in the builder&#x27;s sale agreement before signing?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/check-builder-sale-agreement-before-signing/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Compare the draft with the proforma agreement uploaded on the project's Karnataka RERA page, then check carpet area, total price and what it includes, the payment schedule, the possession date, interest on delay (both ways), how changes to plans are handled, defect liability, cancellation terms and any extra charges. Have your own lawyer review it.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I negotiate the agreement?**: Some clauses, yes, especially commercial terms. Builders often resist changes to standard terms, but it's worth asking for clarity.
- **Is the agreement registered?**: Section 13(1) requires a registered agreement before the promoter takes more than 10%. Registration is through the Sub-Registrar's office.
- **What if the agreement differs from the RERA proforma?**: Ask the promoter why, in writing, and have your lawyer advise before you sign.
- **Should carpet area be in the agreement?**: Yes. The RERA Act requires carpet area to be disclosed. Check the figure matches the RERA page.
- **Who pays stamp duty on the agreement?**: Usually the buyer. Check the current rate with the Department of Stamps and Registration or your lawyer.
- **How long does the builder have to fix defects after handover?**: Under section 14(3), defects you report within five years of handover must be fixed without charge within 30 days, or you're entitled to compensation.

---

## When must the builder register the conveyance deed in my name?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/conveyance-deed-timeline-rera/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Section 17(1) of the RERA Act requires the builder to execute a registered conveyance deed in your favour within the period set by local law. Where there's no local law on it, the deed must be executed within three months of the occupancy certificate. Until conveyance, the builder remains responsible for its obligations under section 11(4).

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What is the deadline for conveyance under RERA?**: The period set by local law. If there's none, section 17(1) requires the deed within three months of the occupancy certificate.
- **Does the agreement for sale transfer ownership?**: No. It's the registered contract. Ownership passes on the registered conveyance (sale) deed under section 17.
- **Do I have to take part in registering the conveyance deed?**: Yes. Section 19(11) says every allottee shall participate towards registration of the conveyance deed.
- **What if the builder hasn't got the OC yet?**: The three-month fallback runs from the OC, so the OC delay itself is the first issue. Section 11(4)(b) makes obtaining it the promoter's responsibility.
- **Where do I complain about a delayed conveyance deed?**: To Karnataka RERA under section 31, citing section 17. Keep your agreement, possession letter and the OC date as evidence.

---

## Corpus fund vs maintenance deposit: what am I paying for and who holds it?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/corpus-fund-vs-maintenance-deposit/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A corpus (or sinking) fund is usually a long-horizon reserve for major repairs and replacements. A maintenance deposit or advance funds day-to-day operations. Until the association takes over, the promoter often holds both. RERA sections 11 and 17 push formation of the association and handover of common areas and documents. Get a written account of unspent balances.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is corpus the same as advance maintenance?**: No. Corpus is usually a capital reserve. Advance maintenance funds day-to-day operations. Your agreement and bye-laws control the labels and uses. Read those, not a generic glossary.
- **Can the builder spend my corpus on finishing construction?**: Corpus is collected as a reserve for the association, not as construction money. Section 11(4)(g) keeps the promoter liable for outgoings it collected but did not pay, and section 17 requires handover to the association. Ask for ledgers, and get a lawyer's reading for your facts.
- **When should the association hold the funds?**: Once the association is formed and common areas / maintenance are taken over under the project's documents and RERA handover duties. Until then, insist on transparent ledgers even if the promoter still holds the bank accounts.
- **Are there official rupee caps for corpus in Karnataka?**: We haven't found an official cap in public sources. Go by your cost sheet, agreement and association bye-laws.
- **What if the builder delays association handover?**: RERA sections 11 and 17 create duties around association formation and common-area conveyance / document handover. Complaint and lawyer options are fact-specific. See also check the project on Karnataka RERA.

---

## Are floor-rise and preferential location charges allowed under RERA?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/floor-rise-charges-rera/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** RERA does not ban floor-rise or preferential location charges (PLC) by name. It does require a written agreement with a price based on carpet area and a full breakup. A premium you saw and signed for is normal. One that appears after booking is the real problem, so read every PLC line before paying a token.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does RERA ban floor-rise charges?**: No. The Act doesn't ban them by name. It requires a written agreement in the prescribed form with the price based on carpet area, and in Karnataka the proforma asks for a breakup of that price. Have your lawyer review the clauses in your agreement.
- **Must PLC be shown before I book?**: Insist on it. Ask for a written cost sheet that lists every PLC line before you pay a token. Section 13 caps what the promoter can take before a registered agreement at 10% of the cost, so don't hand over more without the agreement in place.
- **Can the builder raise floor-rise after I sign the agreement?**: The K-RERA proforma says the Total Price is escalation-free, apart from documented increases in charges levied by government authorities. A new premium after signing isn't one of those exceptions, so speak to your lawyer before paying it.
- **Is PLC calculated on carpet area or super built-up area?**: The proforma bases the Total Price on carpet area, but cost sheets differ in how they work out each premium. Whatever basis your cost sheet uses should be written down. Don't assume a formula.
- **Are PLC and parking the same issue?**: No. PLC is a premium on the flat for its floor or location. Parking raises separate legal questions under RERA. Keep them as separate lines on your cost sheet.

---

## What hidden costs should I expect beyond the base price (GST, parking, PLC, maintenance, registration)?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/hidden-costs-flat-bangalore-beyond-base-price/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** On top of the base price, a Bangalore flat usually carries some mix of floor rise and location charges, parking, clubhouse fees, GST on under-construction units, stamp duty and registration, utility deposits, advance maintenance, a corpus fund and legal fees. Amounts vary by project, so insist on a fully filled cost sheet and read it line by line.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Government charges**: GST. Under the CGST Act, construction of a building intended for sale is treated as a supply of service, except where the entire consideration is received after the completion certificate is issued or after first occupation, whichever is earlier (Schedule II, paragraph 5(b)). In plain terms: on an under-construction flat, GST applies. On a completed flat where you pay everything after the completion certificate, it generally doesn't. The applicable rate depends on the unit's category, so get the GST line written on your cost sheet and check it with your CA rather than relying on a verbal figure. Our page on GST on a new flat: the 1% and 5% rates and when it is zero explains the categories.
- **Is GST payable on a ready-to-move flat in Bangalore?**: Generally not, if the entire price is paid after the completion certificate is issued (or after first occupation, whichever is earlier). If any part was paid before that, GST can apply. Check your specific case with a CA.
- **Can I negotiate parking, PLC or clubhouse charges?**: Sometimes. Developers handle these differently, and launch phases or slow-moving units can have more room. Ask for any waiver in writing on the cost sheet.
- **Who pays stamp duty and registration on a new flat?**: Usually the buyer, as part of registering the sale deed. Check what your agreement says, and check current rates on the IGR Karnataka site.
- **Is maintenance included in the flat price?**: Usually not. Most developers collect advance maintenance separately, often at possession. Ask how many months and at what rate.
- **How can a consultant help with hidden costs?**: By asking for every line in writing, comparing projects on the same basis, and pointing out charges you hadn't thought to ask about. They can't tell you current tax rates with authority; check those with official sources or a CA.

---

## Can a builder raise the price after booking?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/price-escalation-clause-legal/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Not freely, once you have a registered agreement for sale. Karnataka RERA's proforma agreement calls the total price escalation-free, except for new or higher charges imposed by a competent authority, tax changes and a carpet-area recalculation after the occupancy certificate. Your own signed agreement decides, so read its price clauses before paying more than the booking amount.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can a builder increase the price because construction costs went up?**: Not under the Karnataka proforma agreement. It calls the total price escalation-free, with exceptions only for charges levied by a competent authority, tax changes and carpet-area recalculation. If your agreement adds a cost-escalation clause, get a lawyer to read it before you sign.
- **Can GST changes increase what I pay?**: Yes. Under the proforma, the amount payable goes up or down if taxes change. But a tax increase after the scheduled completion date, including any RERA extension, is not charged to you. Ask a CA how a change applies to your instalments.
- **Is there a limit on extra carpet area the builder can charge for?**: Under the proforma, the builder can charge for an increase of up to 3% of your carpet area, at the agreed per-square-foot rate, at the next payment milestone. If the area reduces, the excess is refunded within 60 days with interest.
- **Does a price clause in my booking form still apply after the agreement?**: The proforma's Savings clause says earlier documents like the application or allotment letter can't limit your rights under the registered agreement or the Act. Check that your agreement keeps this clause.
- **Where do I complain about an unfair price demand?**: You can file a complaint with Karnataka RERA under section 31 of the RERA Act. Keep the demand letter, your agreement and payment receipts. A lawyer can tell you whether your facts support a complaint.

---

## What is RERA&#x27;s 70% rule for project money, and how do I check it?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/project-bank-account-70-percent-rule/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under section 4(2)(l)(D) of the RERA Act, a builder must deposit 70% of the money collected from buyers for a project in a separate account at a scheduled bank, use it only for that project's construction and land cost, and withdraw it in proportion to completion, certified by an engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does the 70% rule mean my money is safe?**: It reduces one risk: diversion of buyer money to other projects. It doesn't guarantee completion, and 30% of collections aren't restricted by this clause.
- **Who certifies withdrawals from the project account?**: An engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant in practice, who must certify that each withdrawal is in proportion to the percentage of completion.
- **Can I see the project bank account statement?**: Usually not directly. You can check the project's quarterly updates on the Karnataka RERA portal and ask the builder in writing whether your payments go into the designated project account.
- **Is the 70% rule part of RERA registration?**: Yes. It's a declaration under section 4(2)(l)(D), supported by an affidavit, filed with the registration application.
- **What if I think the builder diverted funds?**: Raise it in writing with the builder, then consider a complaint to Karnataka RERA under section 31. Bring your payment records and the project's quarterly updates.

---

## The flat is smaller than the agreement says. What are my options?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-carpet-area-mismatch-on-possession/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Measure the flat the way RERA defines carpet area and compare it with your agreement for sale and the RERA project page. If it is really smaller, put the gap to the builder in writing before you sign the possession letter. If they won't fix it, complain to Karnataka RERA; compensation claims go to its adjudicating officer.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a small difference in carpet area allowed?**: The RERA Act itself doesn't set a tolerance percentage. Karnataka RERA's proforma agreement lets the promoter charge for an increase of up to three percent of the carpet area, and says any reduction is refunded with interest. Read your own agreement's clause with your lawyer.
- **Are balconies part of carpet area under RERA?**: No. Section 2(k) leaves out the exclusive balcony or verandah and the exclusive open terrace. The promoter has to show those areas separately on the RERA project page.
- **Can I refuse possession if the flat is smaller?**: That depends on your agreement and the size of the gap. Section 18 lets you withdraw and get your money back with interest when the promoter fails to give possession as per the agreement. Talk to your lawyer before refusing, because it affects interest and EMI timing.
- **Who measures the flat if the builder and I disagree?**: The Act doesn't name one. A signed measurement by a licensed surveyor or architect, done the RERA way, is good evidence to bring to the builder and, if needed, to RERA.
- **Does super built-up area matter for a RERA claim?**: Your RERA claim starts from carpet area, because that is what the Act defines and what the project page shows. If you were sold on super built-up area, compare the carpet area in your agreement instead.

---

## Does Karnataka RERA have a model agreement for sale, and must builders use it?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-model-agreement-karnataka/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes. Section 13(2) of the RERA Act says the agreement for sale must be in the form the state prescribes, and Karnataka RERA publishes a Proforma Agreement of Sale. Builders file their version with the project's registration and must highlight every change. Compare your draft with the proforma before signing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is there a standard agreement for sale format in Karnataka?**: Yes. Karnataka RERA publishes a Proforma Agreement of Sale on its Downloads page, under the Karnataka RERA Rules, 2017. Section 13(2) of the Act requires the agreement to be in the prescribed form.
- **Can a builder change the K-RERA proforma?**: Some changes are expected. The proforma's own note asks promoters to highlight every insertion, modification, deletion and added clause when filing it for registration. Ask your lawyer whether a specific change is acceptable.
- **Does the booking form override the agreement for sale?**: No. Clause 31 of the proforma says documents signed before the registered agreement, including application and allotment letters, can't limit your rights under the agreement or the Act.
- **What if a clause in my agreement goes against the RERA Act?**: Clause 25 of the proforma says a provision that's void or unenforceable under the Act or Rules is treated as amended or deleted to conform. Your lawyer can tell you how that applies to your clause.
- **When must the agreement for sale be registered?**: Before the promoter takes more than 10% of the apartment cost. Section 13(1) bars a larger advance without a written, registered agreement for sale.

---

## Are subvention (no-EMI-till-possession) schemes safe?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/subvention-scheme-risks/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** They can work, but the loan is still in your name. If the builder stops paying the pre-EMI it promised, the bank looks to you, and RBI warns your credit score can suffer. RBI also says bank disbursal must follow construction stages, not go upfront. Read the tripartite agreement and plan for the builder missing payments.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What is an 80:20 home loan scheme?**: You pay about 20% of the price, a bank lends the rest under a tripartite agreement, and the builder pays the interest or EMI until possession or a set date. RBI's housing finance circular lists 80:20 and 75:25 as common names.
- **If the builder stops paying my pre-EMI, do I have to pay?**: Yes. The loan is in your name, so the bank can look to you. RBI warns that delayed builder payments can lower your credit score.
- **Can a bank release my whole loan to the builder upfront?**: RBI's instructions say disbursal to individuals should be linked to construction stages, and upfront disbursal should not be made for under-construction projects, with an exception for some government-sponsored projects.
- **Are subvention schemes banned?**: The RBI text quoted on this page does not ban them. It restricts upfront disbursal and asks banks to make borrowers fully aware of the risks and liabilities.
- **Does RERA protect me if the project is delayed?**: Section 18 lets you withdraw with a refund, interest and compensation, or stay and receive interest for each month of delay. Your loan remains your liability to the bank.

---

# Category: Home Loans, Taxes & Financial Structuring

## When does a home loan balance transfer make sense?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/balance-transfer-home-loan/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A home loan balance transfer makes sense when the interest you save over the remaining tenure clearly beats every cost of switching, such as the new lender's processing, legal, valuation and documentation charges. For floating-rate home loans to individuals sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026, RBI bars lenders from charging a pre-payment fee.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can my bank charge a fee if I move my home loan to another bank?**: Not on a floating-rate home loan taken by an individual for a non-business purpose and sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026. RBI's 2025 Directions bar pre-payment charges on those loans, whatever the source of funds.
- **Is there a lock-in period before I can switch?**: Not for loans covered by paragraph 5 of RBI's 2025 Directions. The rule applies without any minimum lock-in period, for part or full pre-payment.
- **Does the RBI rule apply to housing finance companies?**: The Directions apply to NBFCs as well as commercial and co-operative banks, and they repealed the matching paragraph in RBI's Master Direction for housing finance companies.
- **What if my loan is fixed-rate?**: Pre-payment charges then follow the lender's approved policy, and on a term loan any charge must be based on the amount prepaid. It must also be disclosed in your sanction letter and loan agreement.
- **Will a balance transfer affect my tax deduction?**: Ask your CA. The interest treatment depends on your tax regime and the purpose of the new loan, and this page doesn't cover tax rules.

---

## Why do home loans get rejected, and how do I check before applying?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/cibil-score-home-loan-rejection/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A home loan can fail on you, on the property, or on paperwork. RBI's Fair Practices Code says a lender must give you the main reasons for a rejection in writing. Before you apply, pull your free annual credit report, fix any errors, and check that the project's approvals are in place.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does a bank have to tell me why my home loan was rejected?**: Yes. RBI's Fair Practices Code says lenders should convey in writing the main reason or reasons that led to rejection, for all categories of loans irrespective of amount. Ask for it in writing if you only got a phone call.
- **How often can I get my credit report free?**: Once a year (January to December) from each credit information company that holds your data, under RBI's Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025. The free report includes your credit score and the same detail lenders see.
- **How long does a credit report correction take?**: Under section 21(3) of the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005, the lender or credit company must take steps to update the information within 30 days of your request. RBI allows ₹100 per calendar day compensation if the complaint isn't resolved within 30 calendar days.
- **Can a bank sanction my loan but not release the money?**: Yes. RBI's Housing Finance Master Circular allows a proposal to be sanctioned in the normal course, but says disbursements should be made only after the requisite government clearances for the project are obtained.
- **Are stamp duty and registration included in the home loan?**: Generally not. RBI tells banks not to include stamp duty, registration and other documentation charges in the property cost used for loan-to-value limits, except for dwelling units costing up to ₹10 lakh. Plan to pay these from your own funds.

---

## Delayed project, EMIs running: who bears the interest?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/emi-during-construction-delay-who-pays/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Your bank loan and your builder agreement are two separate contracts. Delay interest under RERA section 18 is what the promoter owes you if possession misses the agreement date. Pre-EMI or EMI you already owe the bank still follows the loan documents unless the bank agrees otherwise in writing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can RERA force the bank to stop charging interest?**: No. RERA regulates the promoter–allottee relationship. Your lender is governed by the loan contract and banking regulation. Relief against the bank, if any, is a separate discussion with the bank or appropriate forum.
- **If I withdraw under section 18, what happens to the loan?**: The promoter's refund obligation and the bank's repayment right both need to be closed out. Your loan agreement decides how the outstanding must be cleared, and the bank may want the refund routed to it first. Agree payee instructions with the bank before you settle.
- **Does delay interest under section 18 start from the agreement date?**: It runs for every month of delay until possession when you stay in the project, under the proviso to section 18(1). Exact start and calculation issues are for your lawyer and the order or settlement you obtain.
- **Is a verbal "builder will pay your EMI" promise enough?**: No. Get any subvention or EMI-support arrangement in documents the bank recognises. Sales chat is not a loan amendment.
- **Should I keep paying the builder after the possession date has passed?**: That depends on whether you are withdrawing or staying, and on what the agreement and any interim order require. Do not decide from a WhatsApp rumour; take advice on your file.

---

## Should I prepay my home loan or invest the surplus?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/emi-vs-prepayment-strategy/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Prepaying gives a certain return equal to your loan's interest rate, after any tax benefit you lose, while investing gives an uncertain one. Keep an emergency fund first, then compare. On floating-rate home loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026, RBI bars banks and lenders from charging individuals for prepaying.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can a bank charge a prepayment penalty on a floating-rate home loan?**: For loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026, RBI's Pre-payment Charges on Loans Directions, 2025 say a regulated lender shall not levy prepayment charges on floating-rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes. Older loans depend on the earlier rules and your loan papers.
- **Is there a lock-in before I can prepay?**: Not for loans covered by paragraph 5 of the 2025 Directions. They apply without any minimum lock-in period and whether you prepay in part or in full, with any source of funds.
- **Is it better to reduce the EMI or the tenure after prepaying?**: Shortening the tenure usually saves more interest overall, while lowering the EMI eases monthly cash flow. Ask your lender for both revised schedules and compare the total interest.
- **Should I prepay if I claim a tax deduction on home loan interest?**: Prepaying lowers the interest you pay, and so the deduction you can claim. Whether that matters depends on your tax regime and income, so ask your CA to work out your effective loan cost.
- **Can I prepay a fixed-rate home loan for free?**: Not necessarily. For fixed-rate loans, the 2025 Directions leave charges to the lender's approved policy, based on the amount prepaid for term loans, and they must be disclosed in your sanction letter and loan agreement.

---

## Fee-only advisor vs commission-based consultant: which model suits me?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/fee-only-vs-commission-real-estate-advisor/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A fee-only adviser is paid only by you, so they have no stake in which property you choose. A commission-based consultant is paid when a deal happens, usually by the developer on new projects, sometimes by you on resale, so there's a pull towards closing and towards partner projects.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Are fee-only advisers available in Bangalore?**: Some advisers offer fee-based work, but it's much less common than commission-based consulting. Ask directly.
- **Is a fee-only adviser more expensive?**: In cash, yes, compared with free developer-paid help. Whether it's worth it depends on the checks you get and whether seller money is kept out.
- **Can a consultant offer both models?**: Some do. Ask which applies to your deal and whether they take developer money on it.
- **Does GST apply to an adviser's fee?**: Fees for services may attract GST. Check the invoice and ask your CA.
- **Is commission-based advice always biased?**: There's always a pull, but disclosure and your own checks keep it manageable. See should consultants disclose developer payments?.
- **Should a consultant tell me their exact commission?**: They may not share the figure, but they should tell you whether they're paid and by whom.

---

## How much flat can I afford on my salary in Bengaluru?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/first-flat-budget-emi-to-income/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** How much home loan can I get on salary? Banks start from take-home pay. SBI allows EMIs of 20% to 70% of net income, depending on slab, and the RBI says banks typically count 55–60% of disposable income. Existing EMIs come off first. Then the LTV cap and your cash for the down payment and charges set the flat price.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How much home loan can I get on a ₹1 lakh salary?**: It depends on your lender's EMI-to-income ratio and existing EMIs. With no other loans, an illustrative 50% ratio gives a ₹50,000 EMI, which supports about ₹57.6 lakh at 8.5% over 20 years. At 40% it's about ₹46 lakh. Ask for an in-principle sanction for your exact figure.
- **Is it based on gross salary or take-home pay?**: Mostly take-home pay. SBI uses net monthly income after tax and payroll deductions. The RBI notes that some banks use gross income instead, so ask your lender which one it uses and what ratio applies to your income slab.
- **Do existing loans reduce my home loan eligibility?**: Yes. Lenders deduct existing EMIs, and often card minimums, before working out room for the home loan EMI. In our example, a ₹15,000 car EMI cut eligibility by about ₹17 lakh at 8.5% over 20 years. Closing small loans before applying can help.
- **Does adding my spouse increase the loan?**: Usually, yes. SBI says the loan amount can be increased by including a co-applicant, since the bank considers combined income. Both incomes then count towards the EMI test. Each co-owner who repays may also claim tax deductions in the old regime, which your CA can confirm.
- **How much down payment do I need?**: At least 10%, 20% or 25% of the flat's value, depending on the loan size, under the RBI's LTV caps. Add about 7.6% for stamp duty and registration on most Bengaluru flats, plus interiors. Banks don't usually lend for those charges.
- **What EMI is comfortable for a first flat?**: There's no official comfort figure. Banks may allow more than half your take-home, but we suggest testing the EMI at about 40% or less, including existing loans, and at a rate 1% higher than today's. If the budget only works at the bank's maximum, look lower.

---

## My home loan is sanctioned. Why hasn&#x27;t the money been disbursed?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-loan-sanction-vs-disbursement/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A sanction is the bank's offer on stated terms; disbursement is the actual release of money, and RBI rules tie it to conditions. For under-construction flats, disbursal must follow construction stages, and money can wait for project clearances. Read every condition in your sanction letter and match it to the builder's demand.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **1. The construction stage hasn't caught up with the demand**: RBI's Master Circular on Housing Finance (RBI/2025-26/16, 1 April 2025), para 4(c), says: "Disbursal of housing loans sanctioned to individuals should be closely linked to the stages of construction of the housing project / houses and upfront disbursal should not be made in cases of incomplete / under-construction / green field housing projects."
- **2. Project clearances are pending**: Para 6 of the Housing Finance circular says banks should ensure borrowers "have obtained prior permission from government / local governments / other statutory authorities for the project, wherever required." It then adds that "while the proposals could be sanctioned in normal course, the disbursements should be made only after the borrower has obtained requisite clearances from the government authorities."
- **3. Your own contribution is not yet paid**: Para 3 sets loan-to-value (LTV) caps. As the table reads, loans up to ₹30 lakh can go up to 90%, loans above ₹30 lakh and up to ₹75 lakh up to 80%, and loans above ₹75 lakh up to 75%. Para 3(b) adds that banks "should not include stamp duty, registration and other documentation charges in the cost of the housing property they finance", except where the unit costs up to ₹10 lakh.
- **4. A condition in the sanction letter is still open**: Every sanction letter carries its own list, and each lender's differs. Look for items such as a registered agreement, any tripartite agreement, a builder no-objection letter, title and technical reports, insurance and signed loan documents. Read the "terms and conditions" and "pre-disbursement conditions" sections line by line and tick off what you have submitted, with dates.
- **5. The terms changed after sanction**: The Fair Practices Code says lenders "should give notice of any change in the terms and conditions including interest rates, service charges etc." and "should also ensure that changes in interest rates and charges are effected only prospectively." If the bank says it needs a revised sanction before releasing money, ask for the change in writing and compare it with the original letter.
- **Is a home loan sanction letter a guarantee that the bank will pay?**: No. It records the amount and terms the bank has offered. RBI's Fair Practices Code asks lenders to disburse on time "in conformity with the terms and conditions governing such sanction", so open conditions can hold the money.
- **Can the bank release my whole loan to the builder in one go?**: Not for an under-construction project. RBI's Housing Finance circular says upfront disbursal "should not be made in cases of incomplete / under-construction / green field housing projects", with a narrow exception for some Government or statutory authority projects.
- **Does the loan cover stamp duty and registration?**: Generally no. RBI tells banks not to include stamp duty, registration and documentation charges in the property cost they finance, except where the unit costs up to ₹10 lakh. Budget for these yourself.
- **If the bank is late, do I still owe the builder interest?**: Possibly. RERA section 19(6) and (7) put payment on the allottee as per the agreement, with interest for delay. Section 19(8) allows reduction only by mutual agreement. Get any waiver in writing.
- **Can the bank change my interest rate after sanction?**: The Fair Practices Code requires notice of changes to terms, including interest rates, and says rate and charge changes should be effected only prospectively. Check your loan agreement's reset clause.

---

## What home loan tax deductions remain under the Income-tax Act, 2025?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-loan-tax-benefit-new-act-2025/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the home loan tax benefit survives with new section numbers. In the old regime you can claim up to ₹2 lakh of interest on a self-occupied home (section 22) and up to ₹1.5 lakh of principal, stamp duty and registration (section 123, shared). In the default new regime, the self-occupied interest deduction isn't available.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is section 24(b) still available after April 2026?**: The deduction is, under a new number. From 1 April 2026, interest on a home loan is deducted under section 22 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. For a self-occupied home the cap is still ₹2 lakh a year, in the old regime only. A let-out home has no cap on the interest deduction.
- **Can I claim home loan principal under the new Act?**: Yes, in the old regime. Principal repayment, plus stamp duty and registration in the year paid, counts under section 123 and Schedule XV. It shares the ₹1.5 lakh limit with PF, life insurance and similar items. The new regime doesn't allow it.
- **Does the new tax regime give any home loan benefit?**: Not for a home you live in. For a let-out home, interest still reduces the rental income, but any resulting loss can't be set off against salary or other income in the new regime. Compare both regimes with your CA before choosing.
- **Can I still claim 80EEA?**: Only if your loan was sanctioned between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022 and you meet its other conditions. It's now section 131 of the 2025 Act, with a ₹1.5 lakh limit. New loans don't qualify, so don't count on it when planning a purchase.
- **What happens if I sell the flat within five years?**: The principal, stamp duty and registration deductions under section 123 are reversed. Under Schedule XV para 4, if you transfer the home before five years from the end of the tax year you got possession, the deductions already allowed are taxed as income that year.
- **How much can a let-out flat's loss reduce my salary income?**: Up to ₹2 lakh a year in the old regime, under section 109. The rest is carried forward for up to eight tax years and can only be set off against future house-property income (section 110). In the new regime, the loss can't be set off against salary.

---

## How does a home loan for an under-construction flat work (tranches and pre-EMI)?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-loan-under-construction-flat-disbursement/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Banks usually sanction a loan against an approved under-construction project, then release money in stages tied to construction progress and your payment plan. Until full disbursement, you typically pay interest on the amount already released (often called pre-EMI). Loan-to-value, rates and stage lists vary by bank, so confirm them in your sanction letter.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **When does full EMI usually start on an under-construction loan?**: When your loan agreement says it does, often at full disbursement or a linked date. Read the sanction letter and loan agreement rather than relying on sales talk.
- **Can I get a loan before the agreement for sale is registered?**: Many lenders want the registered agreement before larger disbursements. Section 13 also limits how much the promoter can take before that agreement exists.
- **Who receives the tranche money?**: Often the builder or a controlled payment path named in the bank's instructions, not your personal account. Confirm the payee with the bank for each tranche.
- **Is pre-EMI tax-deductible?**: Treatment depends on the Income-tax Act provisions that apply to you and on whether the property is self-occupied or let. Ask a CA for the deduction that applies to you.
- **What if my builder demands money faster than the bank will disburse?**: That cash-flow gap is common. Negotiate timing, keep a buffer, and don't breach section 13's advance limit to "keep the booking".

## Will banks give a home loan on a Hoskote panchayat or municipal flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/hoskote-flat-loan-panchayat/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes, banks can give a home loan on Hoskote apartments for sale when the papers are complete: an approved plan, an occupancy certificate for a ready flat, clear title and a regular municipal or panchayat record. The risk is the record type. A taxed but unauthorised property has no approval, so lenders may refuse. Ask first.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I get a home loan for a flat in Hoskote?**: Yes, if the papers are complete: approved plan, occupancy certificate for a ready flat, clear title and a regular property record. Hoskote being outside GBA doesn't stop a loan by itself. Get the lender's in-principle approval for the specific property first.
- **Is Hoskote a TMC or a CMC?**: The Bengaluru Rural district website lists the Hosakote City Municipal Council. Villages around the town are under gram panchayats. Check which body issued the property record you're shown.
- **Will banks lend on a Form 11B or unauthorised property?**: We couldn't find a published lender rule. Karnataka's law says paying tax on an unauthorised property confers no title or approval, so expect most banks to be cautious. Ask the bank in writing before you pay.
- **What documents does a bank need for a Hoskote flat?**: SBI lists construction permission, the allotment letter or agreement, an occupancy certificate for ready flats, tax and utility bills, the approved plan, the builder's development agreement and payment receipts. Lenders also run their own title check.
- **Does the loan cover stamp duty in Hoskote?**: No, for homes above ₹10 lakh. RBI excludes stamp duty and registration from the cost used for the loan. Outside GBA, those charges total 7.65%, so on ₹60 lakh you'd pay ₹4,59,000 in cash.
- **What is the LEND check?**: It's our four-part loan readiness check: layout and plan approval, the property extract, the occupancy certificate, and a clean deed chain. If any one fails, a bank is likely to ask questions.

## Joint home loan with your spouse: how do co-ownership and tax deductions work?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/joint-home-loan-co-owner-rules/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** The joint home loan tax benefit works per person. Under section 24 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, each co-owner with a defined share is taxed separately and gets the self-occupied relief individually. So in the old regime, each spouse who owns a share and pays the EMI can claim up to ₹2 lakh of interest and ₹1.5 lakh of principal.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can both husband and wife claim the ₹2 lakh home loan interest deduction?**: Yes, if both co-own the flat with defined shares, both repay the loan and both file in the old regime. Section 24 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 computes each co-owner's income separately and gives each the self-occupied relief, so each has their own ₹2 lakh interest cap.
- **Do I need to be a co-owner to claim the interest deduction?**: In general, yes. Interest is deducted while computing income from house property under section 22, and that income belongs to the owner. A co-borrower who isn't on the sale deed has no house-property share to deduct it from. Check your case with a CA.
- **How are deductions split in a joint home loan?**: By ownership share for interest, and by what each person actually repays for principal. Write the shares in the sale deed, and pay EMIs in the same ratio from each person's account, so the split is clear if the tax department asks.
- **Does adding my wife's name reduce stamp duty in Karnataka?**: No. Karnataka's conveyance rates don't change with the buyer's gender, so a flat above ₹45 lakh in Bengaluru still costs about 7.6% in duty, cess, surcharge and registration. The benefit of a joint name is on the tax and loan side, not stamp duty.
- **What if one spouse is in the new tax regime?**: That spouse gets no deduction for interest or principal on a self-occupied home, because section 202 removes both. The other spouse can still claim their share in the old regime. Run both regimes for both of you before deciding the ownership split.
- **Can a parent and child take a joint home loan and both claim?**: The co-ownership rule in section 24 applies to any co-owners with definite shares, not just spouses. So a parent and child who both own and repay can each claim within their own limits, subject to the lender's age and income rules. Confirm with your CA.

---

## Can NRIs pay for a Bengaluru flat from NRE or NRO, and take the money back later?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-nre-nro-payment-repatriation/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes to both, with conditions. RBI lets NRIs and OCIs pay through banking channels, by inward remittance or from NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO accounts, but not with traveller's cheques or foreign currency notes. When you sell, your bank can let the proceeds go abroad if you paid in foreign exchange or from NRE/FCNR(B), for up to two residential properties.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can an NRI buy a flat in India using an NRO account?**: Yes. RBI's Master Direction allows payment by debit to an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO account, or by inward remittance through banking channels. NRO money doesn't count for the two-property repatriation route when you sell.
- **How many properties can an NRI repatriate sale proceeds for?**: For residential property, RBI restricts repatriation under the foreign exchange route to not more than two properties. The purchase must have been paid in foreign exchange through banking channels or from NRE or FCNR(B) funds.
- **Can I pay the builder in cash or foreign currency notes?**: No. RBI says payments cannot be made by traveller's cheque or foreign currency notes. They have to come through banking channels, from abroad or from your NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO account.
- **Do home loan EMIs paid from NRE count for repatriation?**: Yes. If the property was bought with a housing loan and the EMIs were paid from remittances from abroad or from NRE/FCNR(B), RBI says those repayments may be treated as equivalent to foreign exchange received.
- **How much can an NRI send abroad from an NRO account?**: Up to USD 1 million per financial year, out of NRO balances, sale proceeds of assets or inherited assets, on documentary evidence and after applicable taxes. Above that you need RBI's prior approval.

---

## How much of a flat's sale proceeds can an NRI repatriate?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-repatriation-sale-proceeds/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under the RBI's NRI repatriation property sale rules, you can send abroad, on the property route, up to what you originally paid in foreign exchange, for no more than two homes. The rest goes into your NRO account and can be remitted up to USD 1 million per financial year, after tax. Your purchase records decide the split.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can an NRI repatriate the full sale price of a flat?**: On the property route, only up to the amount originally paid in foreign exchange, for up to two homes. The rest, including the gain, can go via the NRO account within USD 1 million a financial year.
- **What if I bought the flat while I was resident in India?**: The RBI's remittance rules point you to the USD 1 million per financial year route from your NRO account, after tax. Your bank will ask for the sale documents and tax forms.
- **Do home loan repayments count as foreign exchange paid?**: Yes, to the extent you repaid the loan from inward remittances or your NRE or FCNR(B) account. Repayments from NRO funds such as rent don't count for the property route.
- **What is Form 145?**: It's the new number for Form 15CA under the Income-tax Rules 2026, the remitter's statement for payments abroad. Form 146 replaced Form 15CB, the accountant's certificate.
- **How much TDS does the buyer deduct from an NRI seller?**: From 1 April 2026, TDS under Section 393 is at rates in force on the taxable amount, with no ₹50 lakh threshold. Your CA can work out the figure and whether a lower-deduction certificate helps.
- **What is the TRAIL check?**: It's our five-step plan for getting sale money abroad: track payment proof, split the route, count assets, clear income tax, and plan within the USD 1 million limit.

---

## What TDS applies when an NRI buys or sells a flat in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-tds-buy-sell-property-india/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** It depends on the seller, not the buyer. Buying from a resident seller, an NRI deducts 1% under Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, once the price or stamp duty value reaches ₹50 lakh. Buying from a non-resident seller falls under Section 393(2), at rates in force on the taxable sum.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does an NRI buyer pay more TDS than a resident buyer?**: No. The rate depends on the seller's residential status. An NRI buying from a resident builder deducts 1% under Section 393(1), the same as a resident buyer.
- **Is the ₹50 lakh threshold available when the seller is an NRI?**: No. The ₹50 lakh test belongs to serial 3(i) for resident sellers. Serial 17 of Section 393(2), which covers non-resident sellers, has no threshold.
- **Who deducts TDS when an NRI buys from a builder?**: The buyer. The duty sits with the person making the payment, and it applies at each instalment once the price or stamp duty value is ₹50 lakh or more.
- **Can an NRI seller reduce the TDS the buyer deducts?**: Yes, by obtaining a lower or nil deduction certificate under Section 395(1). The application is Form No. 128 on TRACES, filed before the payment. The buyer then deducts at the rate the certificate states.
- **Do I still use the old section numbers for payments made in 2026?**: Not for payments on or after 1 April 2026. Those fall under Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. Ask your CA about any instalment paid before that date.

---

## When does property tax start on a new flat in Bengaluru, and who pays it?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-tax-new-flat-bengaluru/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Inside Bengaluru corporation limits, tax on a constructed building is usually linked to lawful occupancy, often marked by the occupancy certificate, not by booking day. After conveyance, the khatadar or person primarily liable pays on the official property-tax portal. Confirm your PID and demand there, not via a broker forward.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Does property tax start from the booking date?**: No. Booking and agreement-for-sale stages are not the usual trigger for building property tax. Watch OC, khata mutation and the portal demand instead.
- **Who pays tax before I get the sale deed?**: Often the promoter or the association arrangement shown in your agreement still carries dues until conveyance and khata change. Ask for written proof of tax paid up to handover, then mutate khata into your name with your lawyer's help.
- **Can I pay BBMP property tax online?**: Yes, through the Bengaluru City Corporation / BBMP property-tax portal at bbmptax.karnataka.gov.in when your property is within corporation limits. Keep the receipt PDF.
- **What if my flat is still under a gram panchayat?**: Corporation portal rules do not apply the same way. Panchayat areas use e-Swathu / BSK / local panchayat channels. First confirm jurisdiction. See how panchayat property tax is paid for a flat.
- **Are there instalment due dates?**: Under Section 148 of the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024, property tax is due in two equal instalments by end-May and end-November of the financial year, with an option to pay in one instalment and a possible rebate if paid early as notified. Confirm the live rebate rate on the portal.

## How is property tax paid for a flat under a gram panchayat (around Varthur, Hoskote, Budigere)?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-tax-panchayat-flat-east-bengaluru/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** If your flat sits in a gram panchayat, common in the outer belts around Varthur, Hoskote and Budigere, you generally skip the BBMP corporation tax portal. Get the panchayat property ID from e-Swathu or e-khata, then pay via BSK, SAMARTH where enabled, or the panchayat office. Confirm jurisdiction first.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **A. Seva Sindhu / BSK online property-tax service**: The Karnataka BSK online services catalogue lists property-tax payment among property services (building licence, OC, Form 9/11 applications, and tax). Citizen walkthroughs describe:
- **B. SAMARTH Panchayat citizen services**: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj SAMARTH portal advertises tax-payer login, view payable, pay taxes, and print acknowledgement/receipt. Whether your gram panchayat is live on SAMARTH is something to confirm: look for it in the list, or ask the PDO. Do not assume every Hoskote or Varthur village is onboarded.
- **C. Walk-in at the gram panchayat office**: Carry prior receipt (if any), e-Swathu extract, sale deed copy and ID. Ask the counter for the outstanding demand. Payment may be cash, cheque or DD depending on that office's practice; receipt timing differs for cash vs instrument clearance.
- **Can I pay gram panchayat tax on the BBMP portal?**: Usually no. BBMP/GBA portals cover corporation assessments. Paying the wrong authority does not clear your panchayat demand. Confirm jurisdiction before you remit.
- **What ID do I need to pay online?**: Guides to the BSK flow ask for an 18-digit property identification number from the e-khata / e-Swathu record. If you lack it, collect Form 9 / 11A / 11B details from the panchayat or the e-Swathu system first.
- **Is e-Swathu the same as property tax payment?**: No. e-Swathu is the RDPR property-record system that issues Forms 9 / 11A / 11B. Tax payment is a separate step on BSK, SAMARTH or at the office, using those records.
- **What if my area was recently merged into the corporation?**: Jurisdiction can change after notifications. Re-check whether your PID moved to the corporation portal. Do not assume last year's panchayat receipt still matches this year's assessing authority.
- **Can the builder pay panchayat tax for all flats?**: Sometimes during construction or early handover. Get written receipts naming your unit. After sale deed and name change, expect to pay yourself unless the association has a documented bulk arrangement.

---

## How much down payment do I need? RBI&#x27;s loan-to-value limits explained

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rbi-ltv-down-payment-rules/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** RBI caps how much of a home's value a bank can lend. For loans up to ₹30 lakh the cap is 90%, above ₹30 lakh up to ₹75 lakh it is 80%, and above ₹75 lakh it is 75%. You pay the rest yourself, plus stamp duty and registration, which banks can't count in the property's value.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I get a 100% home loan in India?**: Not from a bank under RBI's LTV limits. The highest cap is 90%, for loans up to ₹30 lakh, and stamp duty and registration can't be counted in the property's cost unless the dwelling costs ₹10 lakh or less.
- **Is the down payment 20% for every home loan?**: No. Under RBI's limits for banks it is at least 10% for loans up to ₹30 lakh, 20% for loans above ₹30 lakh up to ₹75 lakh, and 25% for loans above ₹75 lakh. Your bank can ask for more.
- **Is the LTV slab based on the flat's price or the loan amount?**: The RBI table is set out by the size of the individual housing loan. Work out the loan first, then check which slab it falls in.
- **Does the bank count stamp duty in the property's value?**: Not for most flats. RBI tells banks not to include stamp duty, registration and other documentation charges in the property cost, except where the dwelling costs ₹10 lakh or less.
- **Do these limits apply to housing finance companies?**: This circular is addressed to scheduled commercial banks, excluding regional rural banks. Housing finance companies follow separate rules, so ask your lender which limits it uses.

---

## How does a home loan for a resale flat differ from a new flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/resale-flat-home-loan-process/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A resale flat is already built and owned by someone else, so there are no construction stages to pay against. The bank's checks move to the seller and the building: title, the sanctioned plan and completion certificate, any loan the seller still owes, and a valuation. RBI's rules let banks finance an old house.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I get a home loan for a 15-year-old flat?**: RBI's Master Circular lets banks finance purchase of a dwelling unit, including an old house. Each bank then applies its own policy on building age and remaining tenure. Ask your lender for its rule in writing before you agree a price.
- **Will the bank pay the seller directly?**: Ask your lender. A resale flat has no construction stages, so the bank will set out when it releases the money and to whom, which may include the seller's bank if a loan is still open. Get the payee details in writing before registration.
- **What if the resale flat has no completion certificate?**: RBI's para 2(B)(vii)(d) asks you to declare that the flat was built as per the sanctioned plan and "as far as possible has a completion certificate also". Without one, that declaration is harder to make honestly, so talk to your lawyer before paying any advance.
- **How long can the seller's bank take to return the original documents?**: RBI's 2023 direction says lenders must release original property documents and remove registered charges within 30 days of full repayment. If the delay is the lender's fault, it owes ₹5,000 for each day of delay.
- **Does the bank lend on the price I agreed with the seller?**: The bank lends against its own valuation, done under its Board-approved valuation policy, and within RBI's limit on loan amount against property value. If its valuation comes in lower, you fund the gap.

---

## How does TDS on property purchase work from 1 April 2026?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/tds-on-flat-purchase-section-393-form-141/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** For payments made on or after 1 April 2026, a buyer deducts TDS on a property purchase under Section 393(1), Table serial 3(i), of the Income-tax Act, 2025. The rate is 1% of the price or the stamp duty value, whichever is higher, once either reaches ₹50 lakh. The buyer reports it on Form 141, Schedule B.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is TDS on property still 1% after the new Income-tax Act?**: Yes, for a resident seller. Section 393(1), Table serial 3(i), keeps the rate at 1%, now calculated on the higher of the consideration and the stamp duty value.
- **I paid one instalment in March 2026 and another in May. Which law applies?**: The March payment falls under the 1961 Act and Form 26QB. The May payment falls under the 2025 Act and Form 141. The department's rule turns on the date of the earlier of credit or payment.
- **Does TDS apply if the flat costs less than ₹50 lakh?**: Not under this serial, as long as both the price and the stamp duty value are below ₹50 lakh. If either reaches ₹50 lakh, it applies.
- **Does an NRI seller change any of this?**: Yes. Section 393(1) covers payments to residents. Payments to non-residents fall under a different part of the section with different rules, so take advice from a CA before paying an NRI seller.
- **Who deducts TDS when I buy from a builder?**: You, the buyer. The builder is the payee, and the duty to deduct sits with the person making the payment.
- **Which certificate do I give the seller now?**: Form No. 132, which you download from TRACES after your Form 141 is processed. The department's note says to issue it within 15 days of the Form 141 due date.

---

# Category: Title, Approvals & Municipal Records (BBMP/Kaveri)

## How do you transfer BESCOM and BWSSB connections to your name after a resale?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/bescom-bwssb-name-transfer-resale/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** For BESCOM name change online inside GBA, finish your e-Khata mutation first. BESCOM then texts you a link. You log in, check the details pulled from GBA, pay ₹100, e-sign the indemnity bond for ₹1,194 and authenticate with Aadhaar. For water, apply on BWSSB's transfer portal for ₹250.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Worked example 2: dues you could inherit**: Illustrative. Suppose the seller's last three electricity bills were ₹2,800, ₹3,100 and ₹2,950 and unpaid, and two water bills of ₹900 each were unpaid.
- **How do I change the name on a BESCOM connection online?**: Inside GBA, get your e-Khata mutated first. BESCOM then sends an SMS link. Log in with an OTP, check the details pulled from GBA, pay ₹100, e-sign the agreement and indemnity bond for ₹1,194 and authenticate with Aadhaar. Your name shows from the next bill.
- **How much does BESCOM name change cost?**: About ₹1,294 on the online route: ₹100 processing and ₹1,194 for the e-stamp and e-sign, as reported in April 2026. Applying yourself avoids middlemen, who were reported to charge over ₹10,000 before.
- **How do I transfer a BWSSB water connection to my name?**: Apply on BWSSB's Transfer of Connection/Ownership portal with your RR number and pay ₹250. The guarantee is 10 days. If there's been extra construction since the connection was sanctioned, apply through the Online Water Connection portal instead.
- **Do I need the e-Khata before transferring BESCOM?**: For the faceless route inside GBA, yes. It runs off the e-Khata database, and the SMS arrives after mutation. Outside GBA, or if you can't use the link, apply through BESCOM's subdivision and follow its document list.
- **Who pays unpaid electricity and water bills after a resale?**: Agree it in the sale agreement. Ask the seller for the latest paid bills and make clearing arrears up to handover a condition of the final payment. Check the first bill in your name for any carried-over amount.
- **Can I transfer a connection in a deceased parent's name?**: BESCOM's online route also covers transfers from deceased parents to children, per the April 2026 report. Your e-Khata must first be mutated to you, which may need succession documents. Ask a lawyer if heirs disagree.

## When does a new flat get a permanent BESCOM connection?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/bescom-permanent-power-new-flat/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Permanent BESCOM supply is a separate service from temporary construction power. Temporary supply is surrendered before a permanent installation is arranged. After the permanent installation is serviced, BESCOM assigns an R.R. number painted on the meter board. Exact connection charges sit on the BESCOM subdivision demand letter, not on third-party tables.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can temporary construction power be converted into permanent supply?**: BESCOM FAQ material says temporary must be surrendered before permanent is installed; it is not a simple in-place conversion. Treat surrender-then-fresh-permanent as the working rule unless a current official circular says otherwise for your case.
- **When do I get an R.R. number?**: After the installation is serviced. The Conditions of Supply require an R.R. number to be assigned and painted on the meter board immediately after servicing. Quote it on later BESCOM correspondence.
- **Who usually applies in an apartment project, me or the builder?**: Often the promoter applies for bulk / project supply during construction and early handover; individual flat applications (if used) may follow under association rules. Confirm who the applicant is in writing before you pay any "BESCOM" amount on a cost sheet.
- **Are online schedule-of-charges tables final?**: No. BESCOM FAQ text says those charges are indicative; actual payment follows the SDO demand letter. Don't rely on a rupee figure until you have that letter.
- **Does an OC guarantee permanent BESCOM supply?**: No. OC is a building / occupancy gate. Permanent electricity still needs BESCOM service of the installation. See also OC / CC importance.

## What civic body and water supply apply to Budigere Cross apartments?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/budigere-cross-water-and-civic-status/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Most Budigere Cross apartments sit under gram panchayats in Bengaluru East taluk, not a city corporation. Records live on e-Swathu, stamp charges total 7.65% rather than 7.6%, and the area isn't on Cauvery Stage 5. So Budigere Cross water supply usually means borewells and tankers unless a project can show a piped source in writing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is Budigere Cross under BBMP or GBA?**: Mostly not. On our lookup, only about 7% of PIN 560049 is inside GBA limits. Most apartments sit in gram panchayat villages of Bengaluru East taluk. Check the village and survey number for the specific project.
- **Does Budigere Cross get Cauvery water?**: Not through Cauvery Stage 5, which serves the 110 villages added to the city in 2007. We found no public piped scheme for the area. Expect borewells and tankers unless a project shows a piped source in writing.
- **Where do I find property records for a Budigere Cross flat?**: On e-Swathu, the panchayat property portal, not the city's e-Khata. Check whether the record is Form 9 or 11A, which covers regular property, or 11B, which doesn't confer approval.
- **Are stamp charges higher outside the city?**: Slightly. The surcharge on stamp duty is 3% in panchayat areas against 2% in the city, so total charges are 7.65% instead of 7.6%. On ₹80 lakh, that's ₹4,000 more.
- **Do borewells in Budigere Cross need permission?**: Yes. The Karnataka Ground Water Authority handles registration of existing borewells and permission for new ones through its portal. Ask the project or association to show the permission.
- **What is the WARD check?**: It's our four-part check for an apartment outside the city: which body runs it, what approvals it has, what records exist and where the drinking water comes from.
