## How does a new apartment get a BWSSB water connection, and what does it cost buyers?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/bwssb-connection-new-apartment/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** New apartment BWSSB connections usually go through the Board's online service: register, buy the application, upload papers, use a BWSSB-registered plumber, await inspection, then pay the official demand note. The exact charges sit on that note, not on blog tables. Ask whether the promoter already holds a bulk connection.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Do I apply flat-wise or does the builder take a bulk connection?**: Many apartment projects take a bulk BWSSB connection to the premises; individual flat billing then follows association rules. Confirm in writing which model your project uses before you pay a "BWSSB charge" on the cost sheet.
- **Must I use a BWSSB-registered plumber?**: Yes for the online new-connection flow described in Board FAQs: only a BWSSB-registered plumber is entertained, and a consumer–plumber agreement scan is attached before final payment.
- **When do I pay the big connection charges?**: After inspection, when AE/JE calculations produce a demand note and AEE approval triggers an SMS to log in and pay. Do not pay large "connection" sums to a private agent off-portal.
- **Are blog tariff tables reliable?**: Treat them as secondary. Official FAQs and the demand note outrank any March 2025 explainer. If the Board portal is down, wait or visit the division office rather than inventing a figure.
- **What if my project still runs on tankers?**: Some projects rely on tankers or borewells until Board supply starts. That is a living and cost risk separate from the connection application. Ask for the water source plan in writing at booking and at possession.
- **Does a September 2025 tariff revision change connection charges?**: Press coverage of the Sept 2025 revision focused on apartment consumption tariffs and sanitary charges for PGs, not necessarily on one-time connection pro-rata. Its effect on connection charges can't be confirmed without the Board order itself.

## How do I check whether an East Bangalore project falls under BBMP or a gram panchayat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/check-bbmp-or-panchayat-east-bangalore/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Check who issues the khata and collects property tax on the project land, and who sanctioned the building plan. A khata from the city corporation (the former BBMP area, now Greater Bengaluru Authority) through e-Aasthi means a city property; one from a gram panchayat through e-Swathu means panchayat. Confirm it from documents on the project's Karnataka RERA page.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **1. Read the project's RERA filing**: On rera.karnataka.gov.in, open the project. Under section 4(2)(c) of the RERA Act, the promoter must file authenticated copies of the approvals and commencement certificate from the competent authority, and under 4(2)(d) the sanctioned plan. The authority named on those documents tells you a lot. If it's a city corporation or GBA document, that's one answer. If it's a panchayat or a regional planning authority, that's another.
- **2. Ask for the khata and latest property tax receipt**: Ask the developer for the khata extract and the most recent property tax receipt for the project land. Note who issued them. For city properties, you can look up records on GBA's e-Aasthi portal. For panchayat properties, the record should be traceable on e-Swathu (here is how property tax is paid for a flat under a gram panchayat). Once you own the flat, see when property tax starts on a new flat in Bengaluru. For a panchayat record, see how to search Form 9 and Form 11B on e-Swathu.
- **3. Check the land record**: On the Bhoomi land records portal, look at the RTC for the survey number. It shows the village and land details. On former farmland, check that the land conversion is in place. How to read the RTC, including kharab.
- **4. Look at the sanctioned plan letterhead**: It sounds basic, but the sanction letter's issuing authority and reference number are a quick tell. Compare it with what the developer says verbally.
- **5. Ask the developer directly, in writing**: "Is this project's land under a city corporation or a gram panchayat, and who sanctioned the building plan?" A straight question deserves a straight written answer.
- **Is a gram panchayat project in East Bangalore safe to buy?**: It can be, if approvals, conversion and title are in order. The checks are different, and loan availability can vary, so do them before you commit.
- **Is BBMP still the right name to use?**: Many people and older documents still say BBMP. The civic body is now organised under the Greater Bengaluru Authority with five city corporations, and its official site still sits at bbmp.gov.in.
- **Can I check this myself online?**: Partly. The Karnataka RERA portal, e-Aasthi, e-Swathu and Bhoomi are all public. For certainty on a specific survey number, get your lawyer to confirm.
- **Does panchayat khata affect my home loan?**: It can. Lenders have their own policies on khata type and approvals. Ask your lender early.
- **Will a panchayat area eventually come under the city?**: Sometimes boundaries are expanded, but you shouldn't buy on that expectation. Treat it as unknown until it's formally notified.

## How do you search a property on e-Aasthi by PID?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/e-aasthi-search-property-pid/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** For an e aasthi search property by PID number, open GBA's e-Aasthi 2.0 portal, choose Search Property, and enter the 10-digit Property ePID. You can also search by ward or by SAS property tax ID. Searching is free; downloading a Final e-Khata costs ₹125, paid online. If it isn't listed, try partial names and the assessment number.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Worked example 1: two ways to apply**: Illustrative. Converting a draft to a final e-Khata with 12 pages of documents.
- **Worked example 2: matching the e-Khata to the deed**: Illustrative. You're buying a resale flat. The e-Khata shows 1,450 sq ft; the sale agreement says 1,250 sq ft carpet.
- **How do I search my property on e-Aasthi by PID?**: Open GBA's e-Aasthi 2.0 portal, choose Search Property, select Property ePID as the search type and enter the 10-digit number. You can also search by ward or by SAS property tax ID. Downloading or printing the e-Khata needs a login with OTP.
- **What if my property isn't on the e-Aasthi list?**: The portal suggests trying partial spellings of the name, parts of the assessment number, and the previous owner's name, then asking a citizen service centre or LPE centre. Visit the ARO only as a last resort. If it's still missing, apply for a new khata.
- **Is the e-Aasthi search free?**: Yes. Searching and applying online yourself is free. Citizen service centres and LPEs charge ₹45 per application and ₹5 per scanned page. Downloading a Final e-Khata costs ₹125, paid online only.
- **What is the difference between the assessment number and the SAS number?**: Both relate to property tax. The assessment number on your tax receipt is used for property tax assessment and is different from the SAS (Self-Assessment Scheme) number. The portal accepts the SAS property tax ID as a search type and suggests partial assessment numbers when names don't match.
- **What is a draft e-Khata?**: It's the digitised record GBA has prepared from older data, before the owner confirms it. Converting it to a final e-Khata needs Aadhaar, tax and utility details and a property photo. Registration needs a final e-Khata.
- **What should I check on the e-Khata before buying?**: That the ePID matches the deed and tax receipt, the owner is the seller, and the area matches or the difference is explained. Also check whether it's A-khata or B-khata, and that it's final, not draft, before registration.

## What is Karnataka&#x27;s digital e-stamp and how do I pay stamp duty online?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/e-stamp-digital-karnataka-flat/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Karnataka's Digital e-Stamp is a government-issued electronic stamp generated after you pay stamp duty through the notified Digital e-Stamp application, typically reached via Kaveri Online Services. You register, enter instrument details, pay online, and receive a unique-numbered stamp stored in the official repository. Confirm live menus on the portal; do not trust third-party "stamp paper" sellers.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is Digital e-Stamp the same as the older SHCIL e-stamp paper?**: Not exactly. Digital e-Stamp is Karnataka's newer fully digital system under the Digital Stamp Rules. Older Stock Holding e-stamp channels are being phased out as the State moves to digital registration. Use only the channel the IGR/Kaveri portal accepts for your instrument on the day you pay.
- **Can I generate a Digital e-Stamp without an agent?**: Yes in principle. Official briefings describe self-service generation anytime after user registration. Your lawyer may still draft the deed text; the stamp is the duty payment, not a substitute for legal drafting.
- **What payment modes does Karnataka accept for Digital e-Stamp?**: The Digital e-Stamp application offers the payment modes it lists at checkout. IGR FAQs for related Kaveri services describe net banking, cards and UPI, and say manual payment is not accepted. Check the live gateway for your instrument.
- **Does paying stamp duty finish property registration?**: No. Stamp duty payment is one step. You still complete Kaveri filing, the sub-registrar slot, biometrics and registration fee payment on the official Kaveri and IGR portals (Kaveri 2.0 registration steps).
- **Where is the original stamp stored?**: Under the Digital Stamp Rules, the Digital e-Stamp stored in the official Digital e-Stamp Repository is the original. Keep your unique number and download path; photocopies alone are not enough.

## What is e-Swathu, and how do you check a panchayat-area flat's record?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/e-swathu-property-records-flat/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** e-Swathu is Karnataka's system for gram panchayat property records. For an e swathu property search, pick Form-9 or Form-11B, then search by property ID or by survey number with district, block, panchayat and village. Then verify the certificate number and use the portal's check on whether the property can be registered.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What is e-Swathu?**: It's the Karnataka Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department's workflow system for gram panchayat property records. It issues and records Form 9 and Form 11 for non-agricultural property, and lets anyone search records, view property status and verify a certificate number online.
- **What is the difference between Form 9 and Form 11?**: Form 9 is issued only for Tahsildar-certified gramathana sites, sites in approved layouts on converted land, and government housing scheme sites. Form 11 is the panchayat's tax demand register entry and can cover other properties already on that register. Form 9 tells you more.
- **How do I search my property on e-Swathu?**: Open the public search page, choose Form-9 or Form-11B, and search by property ID or by survey number after selecting district, block, gram panchayat and village. The property status page then shows owner details, mutations and conversions.
- **How do I check if a Form 9 is genuine?**: Use the certificate number printed on it. Enter it under Verify Documents on the e-Swathu home page and compare the original with your copy. Forms issued after 15 Jun 2013 are digitally signed by the Panchayat Development Officer.
- **How long does it take to get Form 9?**: Form 9 is a Sakala service with 45 days for the panchayat to issue it. A copy of an existing Form 9 or 11 comes within 3 days of applying and paying the fee. Build that time into your agreement.
- **Can I buy a flat with only Form 11?**: You can register with Forms 9 and 11, but Form 11 alone doesn't show the land was converted or the layout approved. Ask why there's no Form 9, check the conversion and approvals, and take a lawyer's view before paying more than a token.

---

## How do you download an EC online from Kaveri 2.0?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/encumbrance-certificate-online-kaveri-steps/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** The EC online Kaveri 2.0 route is simple: log in at kaveri.karnataka.gov.in, start an Encumbrance Certificate application, enter the district, office area, every property identifier and the search period, e-sign with Aadhaar, pay online, and download the digitally signed EC. Fees are ₹10 plus ₹30 for the first year and ₹10 per extra year.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Worked example 2: planning around your dates**: Illustrative. You apply on Monday 2 Nov 2026 for an EC from 2004. Three working days puts it at Thursday 5 Nov 2026, if there are no holidays. If you also need records from the 1990s, plan for at least two working weeks, and don't fix a registration date until both are in hand.
- **How do I get an EC online in Karnataka?**: Log in to Kaveri 2.0, start an Encumbrance Certificate application, enter the district, area, every property identifier and the search period, e-sign with Aadhaar, pay online and download the digitally signed EC from your login. You don't need to visit the sub-registrar office.
- **What is the fee for an EC on Kaveri 2.0?**: ₹10 application fee, plus ₹30 for the first year searched and ₹10 for each further year. A 13-year search costs ₹160 and a 30-year search ₹330. Check the amount on the Kaveri payment notice before you pay.
- **How long does an online EC take?**: For records from 1 Apr 2004 to date, about 3 working days. Earlier periods take longer: 10 working days for the first 13 years, plus a day for each further 10 years. If it's late, you can file a Sakala appeal.
- **Is Aadhaar mandatory for an EC on Kaveri?**: Yes, for the online route. The application has to be e-signed, and the e-sign uses Aadhaar. If that's a problem, ask the sub-registrar office about alternatives before you start.
- **How many years of EC should I check?**: There's no official minimum. Banks and lawyers set their own requirements, often well over a decade. Ask your lawyer how far back the title chain needs checking, and match the bank's requirement too.
- **Does an EC show all loans and disputes?**: No. It shows registered transactions for the identifiers and offices searched. Unregistered agreements, some loans and court cases won't appear, so your lawyer should also run a litigation search and read the full title chain.

## What should I check before taking possession of a new flat in Bengaluru?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/flat-possession-inspection-checklist/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Before you take keys, walk the flat room by room, match carpet area to your agreement, photograph defects, and collect the possession letter, occupancy certificate status, keys, meter readings and NOCs. Under RERA, structural and workmanship defects reported within five years of handover must be fixed free within 30 days. Do not skip a written snag list.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Do I have to take possession on the date the builder sends?**: No. Check the agreement for sale for the possession date and any notice period. If the flat is unfinished or documents are missing, write back listing what is incomplete before you accept keys.
- **Is a possession letter the same as an occupancy certificate?**: No. A possession letter records that keys were handed over. An occupancy certificate is issued by the planning authority. One does not replace the other.
- **How long does the builder have to fix defects after possession?**: Under section 14(3) of the RERA Act, defects notified within five years of handover must be rectified without further charge within 30 days of notice.
- **Should I hire a professional snagging firm?**: Optional. Many Bengaluru buyers do for larger flats. Whether you hire one or not, keep your own dated photos and a signed list.
- **What if carpet area is short at possession?**: Measure using the RERA carpet definition, put the shortfall in writing, and take advice from your lawyer on remedies under the agreement and the Act.

## Form 11A vs Form 11B in panchayat areas: what's the difference?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/form-11a-11b-panchayat-khata/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Form 11A vs 11B comes down to legality. Form 11A is the gram panchayat's e-Swathu record for regular, authorised property. Form 11B records property the panchayat taxes under section 199C: unconverted land, unapproved layouts or buildings without approvals. The law says paying 11B tax gives no regularisation, title, ownership or legal status.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is Form 11B legal for buying property?**: Form 11B is a lawful tax record, but it doesn't make the property lawful. Section 199C says paying the tax gives no right to regularisation, title, ownership or legal status, and the holder can still face action for the violation. Treat an 11B property as unapproved.
- **What is the difference between Form 9 and Form 11A?**: Form 9 is issued only for converted land with an approved layout, government housing sites and certified gramathana sites. Form 11 is the demand, collection and balance register, and 11A is its regular-property version. BSK issues them together as "Form 9/11A" for a ₹100 printing fee.
- **Can I get a home loan on a Form 11B property?**: We couldn't find a lender rule on this. Since 11B confers no title or approval, expect banks to ask for the conversion order, layout approval and Form 9 or 11A, and many may decline. Ask the lender in writing before you pay any advance.
- **How do I convert Form 11B to Form 11A?**: The state enabled 11B-to-11A conversion at panchayat level on e-Swathu 2.0 in April 2026, according to The Hindu. Eligibility details weren't published in that report. Expect to need land conversion and layout approval. Ask your panchayat what it requires in writing.
- **Can a new plot get Form 11B after April 2025?**: No. Section 199C covers only property created before 7 April 2025, and no new entries can go into the separate register after that. Section 199B bars a new khata or PID for any building site without an approved layout plan.
- **How long does the panchayat take to issue Form 11A or 11B?**: The BSK page lets you file a first appeal if the gram panchayat rejects your application or leaves it pending more than 30 days. A second appeal follows if the executive officer rejects it or doesn't act within 45 days. Keep your acknowledgment.

---

## Can I start interiors in my new flat before possession or the OC?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/interiors-before-possession-rules/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Not as of right. Under RERA, the builder offers possession after getting the occupancy certificate, and you take it within two months. Early access for interiors before that is only by the builder's written permission. Even after possession, the model agreement bars structural changes, removing walls and altering the exterior of the building.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can I do interiors before the occupancy certificate is issued?**: Only with the builder's written permission. The RERA Act and the K-RERA model agreement don't give buyers a right to fit-out access before possession, and possession is offered after the OC.
- **How long do I have to take possession after the OC?**: Two months. Section 19(10) of the RERA Act says every allottee shall take physical possession within two months of the occupancy certificate.
- **Can I remove a wall or extend a balcony during interiors?**: The model agreement says no. Clause 15.2 bars removing any wall, including outer and load-bearing walls, and changing the exterior elevation or design of the building.
- **Will interior work affect my five-year defect claim?**: It can make it harder to show whose work caused a defect. Inspect and record the flat's condition before work starts, and report builder defects in writing as soon as you find them.
- **Can I ask the builder for changes during construction?**: Yes, for minor changes. Section 14(2)(i) allows minor additions or alterations the allottee asks for, but not structural changes to walls, columns, beams or floors.

---

## How do I register a flat on Kaveri 2.0, step by step?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/kaveri-2-property-registration-steps/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Karnataka property registration runs through the Department of Stamps and Registration and its Kaveri online services. You typically prepare the deed with your lawyer, pay stamp duty and registration fees as assessed, book a slot, and complete biometrics at the sub-registrar. Kaveri 2.0 screen labels change, so follow the live portal rather than an old screenshot.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is Kaveri 2.0 mandatory for every flat registration in Bengaluru?**: Online services are the State's channel for much of the workflow, but requirements can depend on deed type and office practice. Start from the official Kaveri and IGR sites and follow the SRO's instructions for your instrument.
- **Can I register without my lawyer present?**: Some buyers do, but it's rarely wise for a first flat. Drafting and schedule errors are costly. The portal does not replace legal review.
- **Do I need the occupancy certificate before sale-deed registration?**: Often lenders and prudent buyers want OC clarity, but the exact sequencing is fact-specific. Ask your lawyer for your project; RERA section 17 links conveyance duties to OC timelines for promoters.
- **What if the Kaveri site is down on my slot day?**: Keep payment proofs and application references. Contact the SRO help contacts published on the IGR/Kaveri sites. Do not pay a middleman who claims a private workaround.
- **Are stamp duty and registration fee the same thing?**: No. Stamp duty and registration fee are separate statutory charges. Confirm both on official sources for your deed. Our Digital e-Stamp guide covers online stamp-duty payment.

## What lift and generator documents should our association get at handover?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/lift-and-dg-maintenance-amc-handover/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** RERA doesn't list equipment papers by name. Section 2(n) counts lifts, central electricity and water installations, pumps and motors as common areas, and section 17(2) makes the builder hand over the necessary documents and plans, including common areas, to the association. In practice, collect each machine's approvals, warranties, service contracts and service history.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Are lifts part of the common areas under RERA?**: Yes. Section 2(n)(ii) names lifts, staircases, lift lobbies and fire escapes as common areas.
- **Does RERA list the lift and generator documents the builder must give?**: No. Section 17(2) requires "the necessary documents and plans, including common areas" to be handed over, but it doesn't list papers for each machine. Make your own list and ask for it in writing.
- **Who maintains the lifts before the association takes over?**: The promoter. Section 11(4)(d) makes it responsible for essential services, on reasonable charges, until the association takes over maintenance.
- **Is a generator covered by the five-year defect rule?**: Section 14(3) covers defects in workmanship, quality or provision of services reported within five years of possession. Whether a particular fault counts is a question for your lawyer.
- **When must the documents be handed over?**: As local laws provide. If there's no local law, section 17(2) sets thirty days after the completion certificate.
- **Can our association file a RERA complaint about missing papers?**: Yes. The Explanation to section 31(1) says a "person" who may complain includes the association of allottees.

---

## How do you get the khata transferred (mutation) after buying a flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/mutation-after-buying-flat-bengaluru/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Khata transfer after purchase means getting the city or panchayat record changed to your name. Inside GBA, it runs on e-Aasthi 2.0, which is linked to Kaveri registration. In panchayat areas, it's done on e-Swathu through the gram panchayat. Budget a mutation charge of 2% of the stamp duty you paid, minimum ₹500.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Worked example 1: resale flat**: Illustrative. A ₹90 lakh resale flat pays 5% stamp duty, ₹4,50,000. Mutation charge: 2% × ₹4,50,000 = ₹9,000.
- **Worked example 2: smaller first sale**: Illustrative. A ₹40 lakh new flat on first sale pays 3% stamp duty, ₹1,20,000. Mutation charge: 2% × ₹1,20,000 = ₹2,400.
- **Worked example 3: where the minimum applies**: If 2% of the stamp duty comes to less than ₹500, say on a deed with ₹20,000 duty (2% is ₹400), you pay the ₹500 minimum.
- **Is khata transfer automatic after registration?**: Not always. e-Aasthi 2.0 links Kaveri registration to mutation, and news reports describe automatic approval after a 7-day objection window in clean cases. But you should still check the record has changed, and apply if it hasn't. In panchayat areas, apply at the gram panchayat.
- **What is the fee for khata transfer in Bengaluru?**: The city's khata fee schedule sets mutation charges at 2% of the stamp duty on the registered deed, minimum ₹500. On a ₹90 lakh resale flat with ₹4.5 lakh stamp duty, that's ₹9,000. Confirm the current figure on e-Aasthi before you pay.
- **How long does khata transfer take?**: There's no official service time we could confirm for e-Aasthi 2.0. News reports describe automatic mutation after a 7-day objection window in undisputed cases. Others take longer, especially where documents don't match. Track the application online and follow up.
- **Do new flats get an individual khata straight away?**: Not necessarily. Bulk khata processing for apartments and multi-storey buildings wasn't live when e-Aasthi 2.0 launched in September 2026. Ask the builder or association when the flats' khatas will be issued, and keep your deed and receipts ready.
- **Where do I apply for khata transfer in a panchayat area?**: At the gram panchayat, which updates the record on e-Swathu. The public property status page shows mutation history for a property ID, so you can check when the owner name changes to yours.
- **What happens if I don't transfer the khata?**: The record stays in the seller's name. Tax demands, utility name changes and a future sale can get stuck, since registration needs an e-Khata. Apply as soon as your deed is registered.

---

## What are OC and CC, and why do they matter when buying in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/oc-cc-importance-bangalore/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** CC can mean two things: a commencement certificate, permission to start construction, or a completion certificate, confirmation that the building was completed as per the approved plans. OC is the occupancy certificate, permission to occupy the building. For a ready flat, the OC is the key document.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is CC the same as OC?**: No. The commencement certificate is issued before construction, the completion certificate after it, and the OC permits occupation.
- **Who issues the OC in Bangalore?**: The competent authority for the area. In the city corporation area, that's under GBA; elsewhere it depends on the planning authority. Ask your lawyer.
- **Can I get a home loan without an OC?**: For under-construction flats, banks lend in stages before the OC. For ready or resale flats, many banks expect it.
- **Can I register a flat without an OC?**: Registration may still happen, but that doesn't fix the OC problem. Get legal advice.
- **What if the builder delays the OC?**: Ask in writing for the timeline. If possession is held up, your RERA remedies may apply.
- **How long after the OC must I take possession?**: Section 19(10) says within two months of the occupancy certificate for your unit.
- **When must the builder register my conveyance deed?**: Within the time set by local law; if there isn't one, section 17(1) sets three months from the date of the OC.

---

## The builder gave possession without an OC. What now?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/oc-not-received-after-possession/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under RERA, obtaining the occupancy certificate (or completion certificate under local law) is the promoter's duty, and conveyance timelines are tied to it. Taking keys without an OC does not wipe those duties. Ask for the OC in writing, check the Karnataka RERA project page, and if needed file under section 31 with your lawyer.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can a builder legally hand over keys without an OC?**: The Act makes the promoter responsible for obtaining the OC or CC and for conveyance timelines tied to it. Whether a particular handover without OC breaches your agreement is a case-specific legal question. Ask your lawyer before you treat the keys as full compliance.
- **I already signed a possession letter. Have I lost my claim?**: Signing a handover note does not automatically erase section 11(4)(b) or section 17 duties in the Act. What you signed can still affect strategy. Show the letter to your lawyer before you file or settle.
- **Is a completion certificate the same as an OC?**: Section 11(4)(b) refers to "the completion certificate or the occupancy certificate, or both, as applicable" under local laws. Names and forms vary by authority. Confirm which document your project needs under Bengaluru rules.
- **Does section 19(10) force me to take possession without an OC?**: Section 19(10) requires you to take physical possession within two months of the OC issued for the apartment. If no OC has been issued, that two-month clock has not started under the Act's wording.
- **Can I claim section 18 interest if I took the keys but still have no OC?**: Section 18 turns on failure to complete or give possession in accordance with the agreement (or on registration suspension/revocation). Whether your facts fit is for your lawyer. Taking keys does not by itself prove or disprove a section 18 claim.

---

## Does a possession letter replace the occupancy certificate?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/possession-letter-vs-oc/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** No. A possession letter is the builder's own letter offering you the flat. The occupancy certificate (OC) is issued by the competent authority and permits people to occupy the building. Under the RERA Act, the builder must obtain the OC and make it available to you, and your two months to take possession run from the OC.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a possession letter the same as an occupancy certificate?**: No. The possession letter comes from the builder. The OC is issued by the competent authority under local law and permits occupation of the building, as defined in Section 2(zf) of the RERA Act.
- **Who has to get the OC, the builder or the buyer?**: The builder. Section 11(4)(b) makes the promoter responsible for obtaining the completion certificate or occupancy certificate, or both, and making it available to allottees or their association.
- **When does my two-month possession window start?**: From the occupancy certificate. Section 19(10) says allottees take physical possession within two months of the OC issued for their apartment, and K-RERA proforma clause 7.2 says the same.
- **Does a possession letter transfer ownership of the flat?**: No. Ownership passes through a registered conveyance deed under Section 17(1). Where no local law fixes the timing, that deed is due within three months of the OC.
- **When does the five-year defect period start?**: From the date possession is handed over. Section 14(3) covers defects brought to the promoter's notice within five years of that date, which the promoter must fix free within thirty days.

---

## How do you check the RTC (pahani) on Bhoomi for land under a project?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rtc-pahani-check-bhoomi/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** The RTC check online Karnataka offers runs on the Bhoomi portal. Select district, taluk, hobli, village, survey number, surnoc, hissa and year to see the record of rights. Check the owner, the extent, any kharab land and the mutation entries, then match the total extent with the land area the project declared on RERA.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How do I check an RTC online in Karnataka?**: Open Bhoomi's RTC page on landrecords.karnataka.gov.in, select district, taluk, hobli and village, enter the survey number, surnoc and hissa, choose the year, and view the record. The same portal shows the mutation register and status.
- **Why should a flat buyer check the RTC?**: Because it's the record of the land under the project. It shows who holds the land, how big it is, whether part of it is government B-kharab, and what has changed. Mismatches with the deeds or RERA are worth explaining before you pay.
- **What is B-kharab land?**: Under Rule 21(2) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules 1966, B-kharab is land reserved for public purposes, such as roads, footpaths, tanks, streams or burial grounds. A private owner can't sell or build on it. Ask how any B-kharab inside a project is handled.
- **How do I convert guntas to square feet?**: One acre is 40 guntas, and one gunta is 1,089 sq ft, about 101 sq m. So 2 acres 10 guntas is 90 guntas, or 98,010 sq ft. Subtract any B-kharab before comparing with the land a project declares.
- **Where do I get the survey numbers for a project?**: From the project's RERA page, the title deeds, the joint development agreement or the conversion order. Collect every survey number, because a project often sits on several, and check each RTC.
- **Can I get a certified RTC online?**: Yes. Bhoomi's RTC page links to the original digitally signed RTC and mutation register. Use that version if a bank or your lawyer needs a certified copy.

---

## Builder still running maintenance after possession: what can owners do?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/rwa-maintenance-dispute-builder/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Under RERA section 11(4)(d), the builder must provide and maintain essential services on reasonable charges until the association of allottees takes over maintenance. Section 17 makes it hand over the common areas and documents to the association. If that hasn't happened, owners should form or activate the association, ask for handover in writing, and complain under section 31.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can the builder keep collecting maintenance after the association is formed?**: Section 11(4)(d) ties the builder's role to the date the association takes over maintenance. The association merely existing isn't enough. Forming the association is one step and the takeover is another, so ask the promoter in writing for a takeover date.
- **Is maintenance included in the flat price?**: In the K-RERA model agreement, clause 11 says the promoter's maintenance cost until takeover is included in the Total Price, while clause 7.2 has the allottee pay maintenance charges after the completion certificate. Your signed agreement decides, so have your lawyer read it.
- **Do I have to join the apartment association?**: Section 19(9) says every allottee shall participate towards forming the association. How membership works after that depends on the association's own rules and the Karnataka law it registers under.
- **Can owners stop paying maintenance to the builder?**: Not without legal advice. Section 19(6) makes allottees responsible for maintenance charges as the agreement sets out, and section 19(7) charges interest on delay. Use the complaint route instead.
- **Where can owners complain about a builder that won't hand over maintenance?**: To the Karnataka Real Estate Regulatory Authority under section 31. The Explanation to section 31 lets the association of allottees file the complaint itself.

---

## Can an apartment association go solar under BESCOM net metering?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/solar-rooftop-apartment-bescom/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes. A solar rooftop apartment plant can run on the association's common-area connection under net metering, or share credits with residents under virtual net metering, which KERC's 2026 regulations allow for apartments. Size it to the common-area load, apply on BESCOM's portal after registering on PM Surya Ghar, and claim ₹18,000 per kW in subsidy.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Can an apartment association use BESCOM net metering?**: Yes. Under KERC's 2026 regulations, all consumer categories can use net metering, from 1 kW up to the sanctioned load or 1,000 kW, whichever is lower. Apartments usually connect the plant to the common-area meter.
- **What is virtual net metering for apartments?**: The whole solar output is exported and the credits are split among participating connections by declared percentages. KERC's 2026 rules allow it for apartments' common areas and individual residents, with a 5 kW minimum.
- **How much subsidy can an RWA get for rooftop solar?**: Under PM Surya Ghar, ₹18,000 per kW for common facilities, up to 500 kW at 3 kW per house. The limit includes residents' own rooftop plants, and the connection must serve common facilities only.
- **How much does BESCOM pay for exported solar units?**: For plants commissioned from 25 August 2026, KERC set ₹3.11 a unit with domestic cells and ₹2.34 without, outside the domestic 1–10 kW slab. Virtual and group net metering get 75% of those rates.
- **How do we apply?**: Register on the national PM Surya Ghar portal, then apply on BESCOM's DSPV portal. Pass a general body resolution and get vendor quotes and a terrace check before you apply.
- **What is the PANEL check?**: It's our five-step plan for apartment solar: permission from the general body, the metering arrangement, the payback numbers, subsidy eligibility, and the load and roof checks.

---

## How do you check an apartment's STP and borewell compliance?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/stp-and-borewell-checks-apartment/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** To check the STP in apartments you're considering, confirm whether the law requires one, then ask for the KSPCB Consent for Establishment and a current Consent for Operation, recent treated-water test reports and the plant's capacity. For borewells, ask for BWSSB or KGWA permission, summer yield and a water quality report.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is an STP mandatory for apartments in Bengaluru?**: It depends on the area. Since March 2024, projects with 120 or more units and 80 KLD of sewage need an in-situ STP where sewer lines exist. Where there's no sewer line, the threshold is 20 units.
- **What is a KSPCB Consent for Operation?**: It's the pollution control board's permission to run the STP after checking the built plant. It's renewed periodically, so check that the validity date hasn't passed.
- **What should STP treated water test at?**: Under the 2017 national standard, Bengaluru STPs should discharge water with BOD up to 20 mg/l, TSS under 50 mg/l, pH between 6.5 and 9 and faecal coliform under 1,000 MPN per 100 ml.
- **How do I know if the STP is too small?**: Estimate sewage: flats × people × daily use × 0.8. For 200 flats at four people and 135 litres each, that's about 86 KLD. Compare it with the plant's rated capacity.
- **Do apartment borewells need permission?**: Yes. BWSSB has required prior approval for new borewells in its limits since 15 March 2024, under the Karnataka Ground Water Act 2011. The KGWA portal handles registration.
- **What is the TEST check?**: It's our four-step STP and borewell check: confirm the legal threshold, see the consents, read treated-water test reports, and check the borewells' permission, yield and quality.

---

## What can I do about defects after possession? The builder defect liability period under RERA

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/structural-defects-after-possession-rera/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A defect in structure, workmanship, quality or services that you report within five years of possession must, under Section 14(3) of the RERA Act, be fixed by the builder free of charge within thirty days. If the builder fails, you're entitled to compensation. The duty continues even after conveyance deeds are executed.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How long is the defect liability period under RERA?**: Five years from the date the builder hands over possession. The defect must be brought to the builder's notice within that period.
- **How quickly must the builder fix a reported defect?**: Within thirty days, without charging you. If the builder fails, the Act entitles you to appropriate compensation.
- **Does the five-year period apply to common areas too?**: Section 14(3) covers defects relating to the development, and Section 11(4)(a) keeps the builder responsible even after conveyance deeds. Common-area defects are usually raised through the association. Changes to plans before possession fall under Section 14(2) instead; see can a builder change the plan after booking.
- **Do I need an engineer's report to complain?**: The Act doesn't require one. For structural issues or disputed causes, your own engineer's report makes your evidence much stronger.
- **Does signing the sale deed end the builder's defect duty?**: No. Section 11(4)(a) keeps the promoter responsible for structural and other defects under Section 14(3) even after conveyance deeds are executed.

# Category: East Bengaluru Micro-markets & Site Evaluation

## Should I worry about buying near Bellandur or Varthur lake?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/bellandur-varthur-lake-living-near/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Buying near Bellandur lake or Varthur lake is worth a closer look, not a flat no. Both lakes are over 100 acres, so the full 30 m buffer still applies after the 2026 law change. The bigger risk is low ground: in 2022 the overflowing lakes flooded the land between them. Check the plot's level, buffer and flood history.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it safe to buy a flat near Bellandur lake?**: It can be, after checks. Bellandur is about 906 acres, so the 30 m buffer applies. The bigger issue is low ground, since the lakes overflowed in 2022. Check the plot's level, the buffer line on the approved plan and residents' flood history.
- **What is the buffer zone for Bellandur and Varthur lakes?**: 30 m from the revenue boundary. Under Act 19 of 2026, lakes above 100 acres keep a 30 m buffer, and both lakes are well over that size, so their buffer didn't change in 2026.
- **Did Bellandur and Varthur lakes flood homes?**: Yes. In September 2022 the civic body said the overflowing lakes were flooding the plains between them, and the chief civic commissioner said flooding was localised to about 5 to 6 sq km.
- **Is Varthur cheaper than Bellandur?**: On official values, yes. Most Varthur apartment lines are ₹44,880 per sq m against ₹63,690 in Bellandur. Neither big consultant publishes a market price for either locality.
- **Does a lake view add value?**: We haven't found reliable data on lake-view resale prices in these two localities. Judge it on the specific building: buffer, ground level and how residents describe the lake through the year.
- **What is the SHORE check?**: It's our five-part check for buying near a lake: the lake's size, the plot's height, overflow history, records such as the approved plan and survey map, and evidence from site visits.

## Flood risk on Sarjapur Road and the ORR: how do I check a flat before buying?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/flood-risk-check-east-bengaluru-flat/
**Author:** Arvind Patidar, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Sarjapur Road flooding is patchy, so check the flat, not the area. On Sarjapur Road or the outer ring road, look at four things: flood spots on the approach road, the distance to the nearest drain or lake, how high the basement ramp sits above the road, and what residents saw last monsoon.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is Sarjapur Road flood-prone?**: Parts of it flood and parts don't. The official list is of road points, such as Panathur 'S' Cross and Silk Board, not neighbourhoods. Check the specific flat's approach road, drain distance and basement level instead of relying on the area's reputation.
- **How do I check if a flat floods in Bengaluru?**: Look up vulnerable spots on the Varunamitra map, confirm the drain or lake distance on the approved plan, measure the basement ramp against the road and ask residents about the last two monsoons. A visit after heavy rain tells you the most.
- **What is the rajakaluve buffer?**: Under RMP-2015, as cited by the Supreme Court in 2019, primary drains (rajakaluves) carry a 50 m buffer, secondary drains 25 m and tertiary drains 15 m. The type of drain decides which applies.
- **Does the city flood list cover outer Sarjapur Road?**: No. The 101-point list covers the five GBA corporations. Outer Sarjapur Road falls in Anekal taluk, so you'll need to rely on site checks, survey maps and residents there.
- **Are upper-floor flats safe from flooding?**: Water rarely reaches upper floors, but you still share the basement, the lifts' pits and the approach road. A flooded road or basement affects every resident, whichever floor you're on.
- **What is the GATE check?**: It's our four-part flood check for one flat: ground level of the basement ramp, approach road flood spots, things nearby such as drains and lakes, and evidence from residents and a visit after rain.

---

## Buying near KR Puram or Old Madras Road: what's specific to check?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/kr-puram-old-madras-road-flat-checklist/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Buying a flat in KR Puram or along Old Madras Road comes with four corridor-specific checks: whether the address is inside the city or in a panchayat further east, your real walk to a running metro station, flood points that have filled with very little rain, and whether the guidance value is higher than your price, which raises your charges.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What should I check before buying a flat in KR Puram?**: Confirm whether the address is inside GBA, time the walk to a running metro station, check flood points on the approach road and compare the guidance value with your price. Then do the usual title, approval and RERA checks.
- **Does KR Puram have a metro station?**: Yes. KR Puram has been on the Purple Line since March 2023. The Blue Line's Silk Board–KR Puram stretch was reportedly targeted for May 2027, which would make KR Puram an interchange.
- **Is Old Madras Road inside Bengaluru city limits?**: Only the inner stretch. Further east, villages are under gram panchayats and Hoskote has a municipal council. Check the village and survey number for the specific property.
- **Does KR Puram flood?**: Some road points have. A 2023 KSNDMC report listed KR Puram and Mahadevapura among points flooding at 4 cm of rain. Check your approach road on the Varunamitra map and ask residents.
- **Why would I pay stamp duty on more than my price?**: Stamp duty and registration are charged on the higher of your price and the guidance value. On a main-road line like Hoodi–KR Puram, the guidance value can be above the agreed price.
- **What is the SPAN check?**: It's our four-part check for this corridor: status of the local body, platform distance to a running metro, approach road flooding and traffic, and the numbers on guidance value versus price.

## Living along the ORR: what do noise and air quality data say before you buy?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/marathahalli-bellandur-flat-noise-air/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** If you're comparing Bellandur flats for sale on the outer ring road, test noise and air for the specific flat. The legal residential noise limit is 55 dB(A) by day and 45 at night. The nearest official air monitor, at Kadabesanahalli, averaged about 37 µg/m³ of PM2.5 in one 2019–20 study, near the 40 annual limit.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **What is the legal noise limit for a residential area in India?**: 55 dB(A) during the day (6 am to 10 pm) and 45 dB(A) at night, under the Noise Pollution Rules, 2000. Commercial areas are 65 and 55. The state decides which zone an area falls in.
- **Is air quality bad along the ORR in Bellandur?**: In a July 2019 to June 2020 study, the official BWSSB Kadabesanahalli station averaged about 37 µg/m³ of PM2.5, higher than residential sites at about 26 and close to the 40 annual limit. Check current readings on CPCB's dashboard.
- **Where is the nearest official air monitor to Bellandur and Marathahalli?**: CPCB's BWSSB Kadabesanahalli station, on the ORR belt near Panathur. Silk Board and BTM Layout also have stations.
- **Are rear towers quieter than front towers?**: Usually. Road noise falls by roughly 3 dB per doubling of distance in open ground, and another building in between blocks more. Visit both at night to hear the difference.
- **Does the Blue Line construction add noise?**: Construction along the ORR is noisy while it lasts. Ask residents about night work and check the line's expected completion on our metro page.
- **What is the HEAR check?**: It's our four-part check for noise and air: height and facing of the flat, exposure distance from the road, air data from the nearest official station, and returning at night to listen.

## Panathur Road access and traffic: what should flat buyers know?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/panathur-railway-underpass-access/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Panathur Main Road traffic is the main thing to test before buying in Panathur, Balagere, Gunjur or Varthur. The railway underpass was widened to two vents in November 2025, but the S-Cross junction stayed a bottleneck and the underpass flooded four times between June and October 2026, per news reports. Drive it at peak hour and after rain.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is the Panathur underpass open?**: Yes. The widened two-vent railway underpass and S-Cross junction opened to traffic in November 2025, per the Times of India. News reports at the time said the S-Cross widening was incomplete because some properties hadn't been cleared.
- **Does the Panathur underpass flood?**: It did repeatedly in 2026: in June, in September, when water reached hip level, and again on 16 October, the fourth time in four months, according to news reports. Check the latest monsoon before you buy.
- **How bad is traffic on Panathur Road?**: After the widening, one resident told TOI that 6 km including Panathur and the ORR took 50 minutes, about 7.2 km/h. Test your own route at peak hour on a weekday.
- **Is there another road from Gunjur or Varthur to the ORR?**: News reports describe Panathur–Balagere Road as the only major route for several localities. Residents mention a future road towards Gunjur, but we found no official timeline. Ask the seller for a government order.
- **Should I avoid buying in Panathur?**: Not necessarily. Prices and distances to the ORR are attractive to many buyers. The trade-off is one crossing that floods. If you can't live with that on rain days, look at areas with more than one route out.
- **What is the EXIT check?**: It's our access test for any flat: how many exits there are, whether a rail crossing sits on your route, whether that route floods, and what the trip takes at peak times.

## Which property consultant can help me buy near Marathahalli or Bellandur?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-consultant-marathahalli-bellandur/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Look for a property consultant who works the Outer Ring Road stretch from Marathahalli to Bellandur every week, not just someone with an office nearby. They should know which pockets are walkable to your office, which side roads choke at peak hour and which towers are occupied, and should show a valid Karnataka RERA agent registration.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it better to buy resale or new near Marathahalli?**: It depends on your budget and timeline. Resale gives you something ready now but needs careful title and OC checks. New projects are fewer here, so compare them with nearby areas too.
- **Does a consultant need to be based in Marathahalli?**: No. They need to work here regularly. Test their knowledge with specific questions.
- **Can a consultant help me find a flat near my office on the ORR?**: Yes, that's a good use of one. Give them your office location and maximum commute time, and judge them on how well they stick to it.
- **Are flats near Bellandur lake a good idea?**: It depends on the specific location, drainage and the current state of the lake area. Visit at different times, talk to residents and ask about flooding history. Don't rely on views in the brochure.
- **Who pays a consultant on a resale deal here?**: Brokerage arrangements on resale vary: seller, buyer or both. Ask before you start.

## Who is the best property consultant in Whitefield for buying a flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-consultant-whitefield/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** There's no neutral "best" list, and whoever hands you one is usually selling. For you, the best Whitefield consultant knows the exact pockets you're considering, shows a valid Karnataka RERA agent registration, says plainly who pays them, and will talk you out of a project. Judge every name this way, ours included.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is there an official ranking of property consultants in Whitefield?**: No. The Karnataka RERA portal lets you check whether an agent is registered, not how good they're. Any "top 10" list online is someone's marketing or opinion, so read it that way.
- **Should I use a consultant based in Whitefield or one from elsewhere in Bangalore?**: Whoever works Whitefield sites most weeks. An office address helps less than recent, specific local knowledge you can test with a few questions.
- **Do Whitefield consultants charge buyers a fee?**: On new projects, many are paid by the developer instead, so you may not pay anything directly. Arrangements vary, so ask each consultant how they're paid on your specific project.
- **Can a consultant get me a better deal in Whitefield than going to the builder directly?**: Sometimes they know about inventory or payment plans you wouldn't find alone. There's no guaranteed discount. Compare written cost sheets, not verbal offers.
- **What's the first thing to check on a Whitefield project?**: Its registration on the Karnataka RERA portal: the registration number, promoter name and declared completion date. Then the consultant's own agent registration.

## Which real estate consultants cover KR Puram and Old Madras Road?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/real-estate-consultant-kr-puram-old-madras-road/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Several consultants cover this belt. The useful question is who actually knows this belt. Old Madras Road changes a lot between KR Puram and Hoskote, so look for someone who can explain each stretch, check whether a project sits under the city corporation or a gram panchayat, verify RERA registration and say who pays them.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is KR Puram part of East Bangalore?**: Yes. KR Puram, Old Madras Road, Budigere Cross and Hoskote are on the eastern side of the city, though the outer stretches are some way out.
- **Are projects on Old Madras Road under BBMP?**: Some are within the city corporation area, now under the Greater Bengaluru Authority, and some further out are under gram panchayats. Check each project's documents.
- **Is the metro useful for KR Puram buyers?**: KR Puram is on the Purple Line, which helps for some commutes. Check current stations on BMRCL's website and time the trip from your building.
- **Should I look at plots or flats on this belt?**: Both exist. Flats in RERA-registered projects are simpler to check. Plots need extra care on approvals and conversion, so have your lawyer check both before any token.
- **Do consultants here charge buyers?**: On new projects, many are paid by developers. Ask each one how they're paid on your specific deal.

## Is there a good real estate consultant near Sarjapur Road for new launches?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/real-estate-consultant-sarjapur-road/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes, but on Sarjapur Road a consultant is only useful for new launches if they slow you down at the right moments. Good ones confirm the launch is on the Karnataka RERA portal before you pay anything, explain what an EOI commits you to, say who pays them, and know Sarjapur Road near Wipro from Sarjapur Road past Dommasandra.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it safe to book a Sarjapur Road flat at pre-launch?**: Booking before the project is registered on Karnataka RERA goes against section 3 of the RERA Act, and you'd have fewer protections if things go wrong. Wait for registration, or accept that you're taking a real risk on trust.
- **Do Sarjapur Road consultants get launch prices I can't get myself?**: Sometimes consultants get early access or launch-phase pricing. Whether that's better than what the developer would offer you directly varies. Ask for the written cost sheet and compare.
- **Can a consultant get my EOI refunded if I change my mind?**: They can follow up for you, but refund terms are set by the developer. That's why you want them in writing before you pay.
- **How far along Sarjapur Road does a consultant need to cover?**: Enough to compare the stretches your brief allows. If you'd consider anything from the ORR end to Sarjapur town, they should know both ends well, not just the projects they're partnered on.
- **Should I only look at new launches on Sarjapur Road?**: Not necessarily. Ready or nearly ready flats remove delivery risk. A good consultant will show you both if your budget and timeline allow.
- **Is launch pricing on Sarjapur Road always cheaper?**: Often lower than later phases, but not always cheaper than nearby ready stock. Compare.
- **Is metro coming to Sarjapur Road?**: Check BMRCL's official site for current plans and status. Don't rely on brochure claims.

## How should school commutes shape where you buy in East Bengaluru?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/school-commute-east-bengaluru-flat/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Pick the school first, then the flat. Families comparing schools near Whitefield often find the school run matters more than their own commute, because a child does it for a decade. Time both trips at peak, count the years left in school, and avoid routes that cross the ORR or a railway underpass that floods.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How far should a school be from home in East Bengaluru?**: Think in minutes, not kilometres. Time the school bus or drive at 7:30–8:30 am. Ten extra minutes each way adds up to about 800 hours over 12 school years.
- **Should I buy near my office or near the school?**: Add up both commutes for a year, and give your child's minutes extra weight. In our example, the flat near the office won on raw minutes but lost once the child's time was weighted at 1.5.
- **How do I check a school's affiliation?**: Search CBSE schools on the SARAS affiliated schools directory by district or affiliation number. For ICSE schools, check with CISCE. Don't rely on a brochure.
- **Which routes should I avoid for the school run?**: Routes that depend on a single crossing that floods or jams, such as the Panathur railway underpass, which flooded four times between June and October 2026, per news reports.
- **Can older children use the metro to get to school?**: Where the Purple Line runs, yes, for example through Whitefield and KR Puram. The Blue Line along the ORR isn't open yet, so check our metro status page.
- **What is the BELL check?**: It's our four-part school-run check: bus route and timing, exit crossings on the way, the long horizon of years left in school, and the learning board's affiliation.

## Buying a 10–15-year-old apartment in Whitefield: what wears out?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/whitefield-older-apartment-resale-age/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** In a 10–15-year-old resale flat in Whitefield, the things that wear out are mostly shared: lifts, terrace and bathroom waterproofing, plumbing risers, pumps, the generator and the STP. The builder's five-year defect liability under RERA is long over, so repairs fall on owners. Ask for the lift register, the repair history and the sinking fund balance.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it wise to buy a 10–15-year-old flat in Whitefield?**: It can be, if the building has been looked after. Check the association's accounts and sinking fund, the lift records and the waterproofing history. A cheaper price can disappear into a special levy if big repairs are due.
- **Does RERA cover defects in an older flat?**: No. RERA section 14(3) makes the builder fix defects reported within five years of possession. A 10–15-year-old building is past that, so repairs fall on the association and owners.
- **What lift records should an apartment have?**: Karnataka's lifts law requires testing and maintenance by a registered person every three months, a register of those checks, an annual report to the inspector and a maintenance contract. Ask to see the register and contract.
- **What is a sinking fund?**: It's money an association sets aside for big repairs, such as lifts, waterproofing or repainting. A healthy fund means fewer special levies. Ask for the current balance and what it's earmarked for.
- **Who pays for a special levy when I buy a resale flat?**: It depends on the agreement. If a levy has been voted on but not billed, write into the sale agreement whether you or the seller pays it. Read the association minutes before you sign.
- **What is the AGED check?**: It's our four-part check for an older building: the association's finances, the shared gear such as lifts and pumps, the building envelope's waterproofing, and the documents including pending levies.

---

## Whitefield or Sarjapur Road: which is better for a family buying their first flat?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/whitefield-vs-sarjapur-road-family-flat/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Neither wins outright. Whitefield tends to suit families who want an established neighbourhood, existing metro access and plenty of ready-to-move stock. Sarjapur Road tends to suit families willing to trade a less certain commute for newer projects and, further out, more space for the money. Start from where the earning parent works.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Schools you'd actually use**: Don't count schools within 5 km. Shortlist the two or three you'd seriously consider, then time the school run from each project in the morning. Ask about admission realities directly from the schools.
- **Water and civic services**: In parts of East Bengaluru, water supply can depend on borewells and tankers rather than piped supply, especially in newer or outer areas. Ask each project what the water source is today and what it's planned to be.
- **Jurisdiction and khata**: Whether a project sits in a city corporation area under the Greater Bengaluru Authority or under a gram panchayat affects khata, property tax and sometimes loans. This matters more on outer Sarjapur Road and at Whitefield's edges. Read how to check BBMP or panchayat jurisdiction.
- **Construction around you**: In a fast-growing stretch, expect years of building work nearby: dust, trucks, road digging. Fine for some families, not for others with small children or elderly parents at home.
- **Is Whitefield more expensive than Sarjapur Road?**: It depends on the stretch and project. Prices overlap a lot. Compare specific projects on total cost per carpet sq ft rather than area averages.
- **Which is better for schools?**: Both corridors have well-known schools. What matters is the drive from your flat to the specific school you choose, at school hours.
- **Does Sarjapur Road have metro connectivity?**: Check BMRCL's official website for current and planned lines. Treat any brochure mention of a future metro as a plan, not a service, until it's running.
- **Should first-time buyers avoid under-construction flats?**: Not necessarily, but you take on delivery risk. If your budget can't handle rent and EMI together for a while, ready-to-move is the safer choice.
- **Can we look at both corridors with one consultant?**: Yes, if they genuinely work both. Ask for recent, specific examples from each corridor before you rely on their comparison.

# Category: Property Advisory & Consulting Services

## Is a buyer-side real estate consultancy better than a developer-paid one?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/buyer-side-vs-developer-paid-consultancy/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A buyer-side real estate consultancy firm, one that you pay, has fewer conflicts on which project you choose. A developer-paid one costs you nothing directly but is pulled towards projects that pay it. Neither is better for everyone. If you want no seller money involved and are happy to pay, buyer-side makes sense.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is buyer-side advice worth paying for on a new flat?**: It can be, for a large purchase or if you're short on time. For a straightforward new flat, careful checking yourself with a good lawyer may be enough.
- **Can a developer-paid consultant negotiate for me?**: They can try. Ask what they actually asked for.
- **What should a buyer-side agreement include?**: Fee, scope, whether it's refundable, and a statement that they take no developer payments.
- **Does it matter for resale?**: On resale, brokers are often paid by one or both parties anyway. Ask who pays them on your deal.
- **Do buyer's agents need RERA registration?**: If they're acting in a sale in a registered project and get paid for it, they likely fall under the Act's definition of a real estate agent and need registration under section 9.
- **Do I pay more if I buy through a channel partner?**: Usually not. You typically pay the builder's price. Compare with the builder's direct quote to be sure.

---

## Can a consultant guarantee price appreciation or returns?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/can-consultant-guarantee-returns/
**Author:** Nitin Gupta, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** No. A consultant can't guarantee that a flat will rise in value or earn a fixed rent, because neither depends on them. Section 10 of the RERA Act bars registered agents from misleading representations. Treat any "assured return" or "buyback" as a contract term: get it in writing from whoever promises it, and have your lawyer read it.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Are assured-return projects safe?**: Some pay as promised and some stop. Judge the written terms and the financial strength of whoever signed the promise, not the headline percentage.
- **Is a buyback guarantee enforceable?**: It depends on how it is worded and who is bound by it. A clause in the registered agreement with the promoter is easier to act on than a side letter. Ask your lawyer.
- **Can a consultant promise rent on my flat?**: Not honestly. They can estimate a range from comparable flats let nearby. Ask to see those comparables.
- **What if an advertisement's promise turns out to be false?**: Section 12 of the RERA Act says the promoter must compensate a buyer who paid relying on an incorrect or false statement in an advertisement or prospectus, and refund with interest if the buyer withdraws.
- **What if I have already signed up for an assured-return scheme?**: Keep every document and payment record. If payments stop, speak to a lawyer, and consider a complaint to Karnataka RERA under section 31.

---

## How do I choose a real estate consultancy firm in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/choose-real-estate-consultancy-firm-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Score each real estate consultancy firm on six things: valid Karnataka RERA agent registration, who you'll actually work with, how well they know your target area, how clearly they disclose who pays them, how thorough their document checks are, and what they do after you book. Talk to at least two firms and compare.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Should I use more than one consultancy firm?**: You can, but it can get messy if two firms show you the same project. Tell them upfront.
- **Is a firm better than an individual consultant?**: Not automatically. Check the person you'll actually work with.
- **How do I know a firm isn't just pushing its partner projects?**: Ask which projects pay them, and ask to see options that don't.
- **Does a consultancy firm handle legal checks?**: Most collect documents and flag issues. A title opinion should come from your own lawyer. See legal due diligence.
- **Where can I complain about a consultancy firm?**: If it's a registered agent and RERA rules were broken, the Karnataka RERA portal. For consumer issues, the National Consumer Helpline.
- **How many advisory firms should I talk to?**: Two or three is usually enough to compare.
- **Should I pay for a sample view?**: Many firms will do a short view free as part of winning your business. For detailed reports, some charge.

## Real estate consultant vs broker vs advisory firm: which should a Bangalore buyer use?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/consultant-vs-broker-vs-advisory-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Use a broker when you mainly need listings and someone to close. Use a consultant, usually developer-paid, for help shortlisting and checking new projects. Use a fee-paid advisory firm when you want someone paid only by you. The labels overlap a lot in Bangalore, so judge people by who pays them and what they'll do.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a real estate advisory firm always unbiased?**: No. Fee-paid advisory removes one source of bias, but you should still confirm in writing that they take no developer or seller money on your deal.
- **Do brokers in Bangalore need RERA registration?**: If they're facilitating the sale or purchase of a unit in a RERA-registered project, section 9 requires registration. Resale and rental work outside registered projects may sit differently; ask a lawyer about specific cases.
- **Is a channel partner the same as a consultant?**: Often, yes. "Channel partner" usually means a consultant or firm with a commercial tie-up with a developer. It's a description of who pays them, not a separate legal category.
- **Which option is cheapest for me?**: A developer-paid consultant usually costs you nothing directly. A fee-paid advisor costs money. A broker's cost depends on local practice and the deal. Cheapest isn't always best value, so weigh whose interests the fee buys.
- **Is an adviser legally required to act in my interest?**: There's no specific Indian law making property advisers fiduciaries in the way some financial advisers are. Your protection comes from the RERA Act's rules for agents and whatever your agreement says.

---

## Does a consultant replace your own property lawyer for title verification?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/consultant-vs-property-lawyer-title-check/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** No. A real estate consultancy firm can gather documents and spot obvious gaps, but a title opinion should come from your own property lawyer you appoint. The lawyer reads the ownership chain, checks for encumbrances and disputes, confirms land conversion and approvals are valid, and reviews the agreement. They work only for you.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a lawyer needed for a new flat in a RERA project?**: Yes. RERA registration helps, but title and agreement terms still need review by your own lawyer.
- **Can I use the builder's lawyer?**: They act for the builder. Use your own.
- **How much does a property lawyer cost?**: It varies. Get a quote for the specific job.
- **What if the lawyer finds a problem?**: Ask the seller or promoter to fix it before you pay. If it can't be fixed, walk away.
- **Is the bank's approval enough?**: No. The bank checks for its own purposes.
- **Will a consultant handle registration for me?**: They can coordinate. You or your PoA holder sign at the Sub-Registrar's office.

A nearby office or map pin alone proves nothing.

- **Day 6-7: Joint visit test**: On that first visit, watch how they behave:
- **Is Google “real estate consultant near me” enough?**: It's a starting directory, not a vetting process. Use it to find names, then apply RERA, disclosure and corridor tests.

## What should a first-time homebuyer in Bangalore expect from a property consultant?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/first-time-buyer-property-consultant-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Expect a property consultant in Bangalore to help you turn a vague wish into a clear brief, shortlist projects that fit, explain the paperwork in plain language, check RERA registration and key documents, negotiate, and walk you through the loan and registration. Don't expect them to replace your lawyer, guarantee returns or make the decision for you.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Should a first-time buyer use a property consultant?**: It can help, especially if you're short on time or new to Bangalore. You can also buy directly. The main thing is that someone checks the paperwork properly, and that includes your lawyer.
- **Is under-construction or ready-to-move better for a first home?**: Ready-to-move removes delay risk but usually costs more. Under-construction is often cheaper but carries delivery risk. It depends on your situation.
- **Will a consultant help after I move in?**: Some do, with khata transfer or defect follow-up. Ask what they'll do after registration.
- **How do I know a consultant is trustworthy?**: Check their RERA registration, ask how they're paid, and see whether they encourage you to get your own lawyer.
- **Do budget buyers get less attention from consultants?**: Sometimes, because commissions are smaller. A good consultant treats you the same. If you feel brushed off, move on.

## What does the home buying process look like with a real estate consultant in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-buying-process-with-consultant-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** With a real estate consultant in Bangalore, the process usually runs: brief, shortlist, site visits, document checks, negotiation, booking, agreement for sale, home loan, payments as the project progresses, sale deed registration, and handover with khata transfer. The consultant coordinates and checks. You still make the decisions, sign the documents and use your own lawyer for title.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **How long does buying a flat in Bangalore take?**: For a ready flat, it can be a few weeks to a couple of months depending on checks and the loan. For under-construction, booking to agreement can be quick, but possession can be years away.
- **Does the consultant attend registration?**: Many do, to help with coordination. It's your signature and responsibility, though.
- **Who drafts the agreement for sale?**: The developer usually does. Your lawyer should review it against the RERA proforma.
- **What if something goes wrong after booking?**: Your rights depend on the agreement and the RERA Act. Talk to your lawyer, and read what a first-time buyer should expect from a property consultant.
- **What if I change my mind after booking?**: It depends on the booking form and agreement terms. Read the cancellation clauses before paying.

## How do property consultants in Bangalore get paid, by the buyer or the developer?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/how-property-consultants-bangalore-get-paid/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** On primary sales, most property consultants in Bangalore are paid by the developer when a booking happens through them, not through a separate invoice to you. Buyers often pay no advisory fee at all. That doesn’t make the advice unbiased, so always ask who pays, and get the answer in writing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Do buyers in Bangalore normally pay property consultants on new flats?**: Often they don't pay a separate advisory invoice on primary sales, because developers commonly pay channel partners. That pattern is common, not universal. Ask for your case.
- **Can a consultant be paid by both buyer and developer on the same deal?**: It can happen in messy arrangements. If both sides might pay, you want that stated before you proceed. Unclear double compensation is a trust failure.
- **Will developer payment force them to hide problems?**: Not necessarily, but it can soften pushback. Judge consultants by whether they raise RERA gaps, possession risk and cost add-ons even on partnered projects.
- **Are commission rates public on Karnataka RERA?**: Agent registration and project particulars are what the public portal is built to show. Developer-channel commercial payouts are typically private contracts, not a buyer-facing tariff board.
- **Is acre&amp;key paid by me or by the developer?**: Advice to you is free. On partnered projects, the developer may pay acre&amp;key when a booking happens through us. Ask us again on the specific project you're considering, because relationships differ by inventory.
- **Will a free consultant show me projects they don't earn on?**: Some will. Ask directly. If the answer's no, you'll need to do some of that research yourself.
