## How do I choose a trustworthy real estate consultant in Bangalore?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/how-to-choose-real-estate-consultant-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** To choose a real estate consultant in Bangalore you can trust, verify their Karnataka RERA agent registration, ask who pays them, and see whether they’ll say “no” to a bad fit. Trustworthy consultants explain their fee arrangement in plain words and give you time to read documents before any token.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is a RERA-registered agent automatically trustworthy?**: No. Registration is a baseline legal filter, not a character certificate. You still need disclosure, local depth and document discipline.
- **Should I prefer a big national brokerage over a local consultant?**: Size can mean process and inventory access. It can also mean you're only a lead ID. For East Bangalore self-use buys, a smaller team with corridor depth and clear disclosure often serves you better than a national logo with a rotating caller.
- **What if a consultant refuses to put fee disclosure in writing?**: Treat that as a failed trust test. If they can't write one sentence about who pays them, they're asking you to guess their incentives.
- **Can I work with two consultants at once?**: Yes, early on. Be transparent if both are arranging visits to the same project, so site teams aren't played against each other in a messy way. Once you shortlist seriously, pick one primary coordinator.
- **Does “free for buyers” mean unbiased?**: Not by itself. Free to you can still mean paid by a developer. Free is about your invoice, not about incentive design. See how consultants get paid.
- **What if a consultant refuses to answer about payment?**: Treat that as a no. You're making one of the biggest purchases of your life; you're entitled to know their incentives.

## What red flags suggest a property consultant in Bangalore may be running a scam?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/red-flags-real-estate-consultant-bangalore/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Stop if a consultant asks you to pay them personally instead of the developer, pushes a project that isn't on the Karnataka RERA portal, won't share their own RERA agent number, offers documents you can't verify, or promises guaranteed returns. Any one of these is reason enough. A genuine real estate consultant in Bangalore won't mind you checking.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it a scam if a consultant asks for a booking fee?**: Not necessarily, if it's paid to the developer under a written booking form. It's a red flag if it's paid to the consultant personally or there's nothing in writing.
- **Can a consultant sell a project before RERA registration?**: Section 3 of the RERA Act says a promoter can't market, book or sell before registration, and section 10(a) says an agent can't facilitate the sale of an unregistered project. So no.
- **Are "assured return" schemes legal?**: Treat them with deep suspicion. Get any such promise in writing from the developer and have a lawyer review it. More on whether a consultant can guarantee returns.
- **How do I check if a consultant really represents a developer?**: Call the developer on the number from their official website and ask. Don't use contact details the consultant gives you.
- **Where can I complain about a fraudulent consultant?**: The Karnataka RERA portal for registered projects and agents, the National Consumer Helpline for consumer issues, and the police if money's been taken. Get legal advice on which applies. Also see verifying RERA registration.

---

## Should a real estate consultant disclose if a developer is paying them?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/should-consultant-disclose-developer-payment/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Yes. A consultant who may be paid by a developer when you book should say so plainly, before the first site visit and for each project they show you. The RERA Act has no specific commission-disclosure rule for agents, but it bars misleading claims about services, and you can't weigh advice without knowing who pays.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is it illegal for a consultant not to tell me a developer pays them?**: The RERA Act doesn't contain a specific commission-disclosure clause for agents. It does prohibit misleading representations about services and false claims of affiliation under section 10(c). Claiming to take no developer money while taking it on the same deal can cross that line. Get specific advice from a lawyer if you think it has.
- **Should the consultant tell me how much the developer pays them?**: You can ask, but don't expect it. Payout terms are usually private and vary by project. The direction of payment (developer, you, both, nobody) is the part you're entitled to expect.
- **Does a developer paying the consultant mean I'll pay more for the flat?**: Not necessarily. Pricing depends on the developer's own policy. Compare the written cost sheet you get through the consultant with one you request directly. If they differ, ask why in writing.
- **What if a consultant is paid by both me and the developer?**: Then you should know about both before you agree to any fee. Paying an advisory fee while the same person collects a developer payout on the same unit is something you'd want spelled out in your agreement with them, or avoided.
- **Can a developer-paid consultant still give good advice?**: Yes, if they're open about it and willing to tell you when a partnered project doesn't suit you. Judge them on whether they ever say no, not on whether they're paid.
- **Is an authorised sales partner the same as a channel partner?**: Broadly, yes. Different builders use different terms.

---

## How do I verify a property consultant&#x27;s RERA registration in Karnataka?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/verify-property-consultant-rera-karnataka/
**Author:** Gaurav Mongia, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** Before you rely on any property consultant in Bangalore, get their Karnataka RERA agent registration number and check it yourself on rera.karnataka.gov.in (agent status search). The name, status and validity should all match, and you want this done before any token.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is RERA agent registration mandatory for every property conversation?**: Section 9 focuses on facilitating sale or purchase in projects registered under section 3. If someone is actively facilitating that sale or purchase, registration is the legal baseline. Informal “market gossip” chats aren't the same as facilitation, but buyers should be wary of anyone who brokers a booking while claiming to sit outside the rules.
- **Can I trust a laminated certificate without portal verification?**: No. Certificates can be outdated, altered or belong to someone else. The public portal is the check that matters.
- **Does a valid agent registration mean the flat is safe to buy?**: No. It only addresses the facilitator’s registration status. You still need project RERA review, title/due diligence with a lawyer, cost sheet clarity and sanction checks with your lender if you're taking a loan.
- **Where do I complain if an unregistered person facilitated a sale?**: Use the complaint and contact routes published on the Karnataka RERA portal. Keep your booking documents, messages and payment proofs. This page isn't a substitute for legal advice on your facts.
- **Individual versus firm registration: which should I ask for?**: Ask which entity is actually facilitating your booking and verify that entity. If a firm is registered but a freelance caller is acting alone without a clear link, clarify the relationship in writing.
- **Does a consultancy company need separate registration in each state?**: Registration is with each state's Authority. A firm working in Karnataka should be on the Karnataka portal.
- **How long is agent registration valid?**: The Act sets a validity period and allows renewal. Read the validity dates on the firm's portal record.

---

## What are real estate consultancy services and what do they include?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/what-are-real-estate-consultancy-services/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** For a homebuyer, real estate consultancy services cover the work between "I want a flat" and "I have the keys": setting your brief, shortlisting projects, site visits, RERA and paperwork checks, decoding cost sheets, booking and loan coordination, and follow-through to registration. Firms differ widely, so get the list in writing.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **1. Brief and budget setting**: What you get: A clear written brief: all-in budget (not just base price), must-haves, commute anchors, ready versus under construction, who'll live there and when you need to move.
- **2. Market and locality guidance**: What you get: Honest trade-offs between areas you're considering. In East Bengaluru that might mean Whitefield against Sarjapur Road, or Varthur against Budigere Cross, explained in terms of your commute, schools and stage of development rather than "investment potential."
- **3. Shortlisting**: What you get: Three to five projects that fit the brief, with a reason for each, and ideally a note on what you rejected.
- **4. Site visits**: What you get: Planned visits with a list of things to check, not just a show flat tour. Good consultancies also suggest visiting at your commute hour.
- **5. RERA and first-level document checks**: What you get: The project's page on the Karnataka RERA portal pulled up and explained: registration number, promoter, declared completion date, and any complaints listed. A first look at title, approvals and khata documents to spot obvious gaps.
- **6. Cost sheet and payment plan review**: What you get: A line-by-line explanation of what you'll actually pay: base price, floor rise or PLC, parking, GST where applicable, clubhouse, deposits, maintenance and corpus, stamp duty and registration. Plus a view on the payment schedule.
- **7. Negotiation and booking coordination**: What you get: Help asking for what's negotiable (unit choice, payment plan, add-ons), and coordination with the developer's team on booking forms and receipts. No promise of a fixed discount.
- **8. Home loan coordination**: What you get: Introductions to lenders and help gathering documents. Ask whether the consultancy earns anything from the lender, which is a separate question from developer payouts.
- **9. Agreement support**: What you get: Help reading the agreement for sale in plain English and spotting clauses to raise with your lawyer. Not a replacement for the lawyer.
- **10. Registration and handover**: What you get: Coordination around registration at the Sub-Registrar's office (booked via Kaveri Online Services), khata transfer after purchase, possession checks and snag lists. Under section 19(10) of the RERA Act, you're expected to take possession within two months of the occupancy certificate, so it helps to have someone keeping track. See registration and handover support.
- **Do I need all of these services?**: No. If you already know the area and have a lawyer, you might only want shortlisting and cost-sheet help. Pick what you need and ask the consultancy to be clear about what they'll actually do.
- **Are real estate consultancy services free?**: Often, on new projects, the consultancy is paid by the developer rather than you. Some charge buyers a fee for specific work. Ask before you start. See is a free property consultant really free?
- **Can a consultancy help with resale flats too?**: Many can, but resale needs extra checks on the seller's title, loan closure and khata. Ask whether they handle resale regularly.
- **Will a consultancy check the title of the property?**: They can screen documents and spot obvious gaps. A proper title check should come from your own property lawyer.
- **Do consultancy services continue after I've booked?**: They should, if you've agreed that upfront. Payment plan follow-up, agreement reading, registration and handover are where many buyers need the most help.
- **Does advisory continue after registration?**: Some firms help with khata transfer and handover. Ask.

---

## What does a real estate consultant in Bangalore actually do for a homebuyer?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/what-does-real-estate-consultant-bangalore-do/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** A real estate consultant in Bangalore turns your brief into a short list of suitable projects, filtering on location, budget, Karnataka RERA status, paperwork risk and timelines. They explain the trade-offs, arrange site visits and stay with you through booking and handover paperwork, without replacing your lawyer.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Clarifying the brief before any site visit**: The real work starts before you see a sample flat. A consultant should pin down:
- **Building a shortlist for East Bengaluru**: In East Bengaluru the same ticket price can buy very different living experiences across Whitefield, Brookefield, Kadugodi, Hoodi, Mahadevapura, Bellandur, Panathur, Sarjapur Road, Varthur, Gunjur, Budigere Cross, Hoskote and Old Madras Road. The consultant’s job is to shrink that map to a few projects that fit your brief and be straight about the trade-offs, like commute against quiet, social infrastructure against price per sq ft, or delivery risk against a discount.
- **Checking project and agent basics against RERA**: Before you pay a token, your consultant should help you confirm that the project appears on the Karnataka RERA portal and that the person facilitating the sale is registered where the Act requires it. Section 9 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 requires real estate agents facilitating sale or purchase in a registered project to obtain registration. Section 10 sets out agent duties, including not facilitating unregistered projects and not using unfair trade practices.
- **Site visits that answer real questions**: A site visit isn't a photo walk. You want answers on:
- **Cost clarity beyond the base price**: Buyers lose money in the gap between the advertised base price and what actually leaves their account at registration. A consultant should walk you through typical add-ons and point you to a proper cost sheet from the developer (see hidden costs beyond the base price). Exact GST, stamp duty and registration figures depend on the unit and current state rules, so treat any verbal “all-in” number as incomplete until you see a written working.
- **Booking, agreement and follow-through**: Once you shortlist a unit, the consultant coordinates with the developer’s sales team on availability, payment schedule and document pack. They should push for time to read the agreement for sale, not celebrate a same-day token as a win. After booking, good follow-through means explaining demand notices, sense-checking construction updates and helping NRI buyers who need remote coordination.
- **Do I need a real estate consultant if I already like one project?**: Not always. If you have already done RERA checks, cost math and a lawyer review, you may only need help on negotiation logistics. A consultant still helps when you want a second shortlist or a second opinion and pushback on sales claims.
- **Can a consultant help NRI buyers who can't travel to Bengaluru?**: Yes, many East Bangalore purchases for NRIs are coordinated remotely with video walkthroughs, document sharing and a local Power of Attorney process where needed. The consultant should still insist on the same RERA and paperwork checks you would do in person. See what an NRI needs to buy without travelling.
- **Will a consultant get me a lower price than the builder desk?**: Sometimes they can surface inventory or payment plans you would not see alone. There is no guaranteed discount percentage. Treat any “special rate only today” claim as a sales tactic until it appears on an official cost sheet.
- **What East Bangalore areas does a local consultant usually cover?**: For acre&amp;key, the focus is Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Varthur, Gunjur, Marathahalli, KR Puram, Budigere Cross, Hoskote, Old Madras Road, Panathur, Bellandur, Kadugodi, Brookefield, Mahadevapura, Hoodi and ITPL. Depth in a few corridors beats thin coverage across the whole city.
- **Will the builder give me a better price if I come without a consultant?**: Sometimes, sometimes not. It depends on the developer. Ask for a written cost sheet directly and compare it with what a consultant gets you for the same unit.

---

## What does a real estate investment consultant do?

**URL:** https://answers.acrenkey.com/what-does-real-estate-investment-consultant-do/
**Author:** Piyush Mittal, acre&key
**Direct Answer:** An investment consultant helps you decide whether, where and what to buy as an investment rather than a home. For an individual in Bangalore, that usually means matching your goal (rental income, long-term growth, or both) to specific locations and projects, checking the risks, estimating costs and rents realistically, and planning how you'd eventually exit.

### Contextual Clarifications & FAQs:
- **Is an investment consultant different from a regular property consultant?**: The focus is different. A home buyer cares about living there. An investor cares about rent, growth and exit. Many consultants do both.
- **Do investment consultants charge a fee?**: Some do. Many are paid by developers. Ask. See investment consultant fees and bias.
- **Can a consultant help NRIs invest?**: Yes. NRIs have specific rules on payment and repatriation. RBI's FEMA rules let NRIs buy residential and commercial property, but not agricultural land, plantation property or farmhouses.
- **What returns should I expect?**: There's no reliable standard figure. Be wary of anyone quoting one without detailed numbers.
- **Should I invest in pre-launch projects?**: They carry extra risk. Section 3 of the RERA Act bars a promoter from advertising, marketing, booking or selling in a project before it's registered, so an "EOI" taken before registration sits outside that protection.
- **Can I ask for references?**: Yes, though they'll pick happy clients. Also check online reviews carefully.
